sanskrit_iast: ā vartani madhuneti dṛtireva ca dṛśyate | ardhāṣṭamā apāṃ jñeyā adhyardhāntyāgnidevatā ||
meaning: आ वर्तनि मधुनेति दृतिरेव च दृश्यते | अर्धाष्टमा अपां ज्ञेया अध्यर्धान्त्याग्निदेवता ||
text: The skin itself appears in (the passage) 'Refresh the track with mead'a (a vartanim madhuna: iv. 45, 3°). Seven and a half (stanzas) are to be known as (belonging) to the Waters (16-23 ab); the last in addition to the (preceding) half (23 ed, 24) has Agni as its deity. a

sanskrit_iast: kasya nūnaṃ tu kāryyādyā āgneyyṛk savitustṛcaḥ | bhagamaktasya bhāgī vā paraṃ yaccicca vāruṇam ||
meaning: कस्य नूनं तु कार्य्याद्या आग्नेय्यृक् सवितुस्तृचः | भगमक्तस्य भागी वा परं यच्चिच्च वारुणम् ||
text: But (in) 'Of whom now' (kasya nunam: i. 24) the first (stanza) is addressed to Ka (1), there is (then) a stanza addressed to Agni (2), a triplet (next) to Savitr (3-5), 'Bestowed by the gods' (bhaga-bhaktasya: 5), being optionally (va) addressed to Bhaga. What follows (6-15), as well as (the next hymn) 'Whatever' (yac cit: i. 25), is addressed to Varuna. i.

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣvā hīti cāgneye ṛgagnermadhyamasya tu | jarābodheti vijñeyā vaiśvadevyuttamā namaḥ ||
meaning: वसिष्वा हीति चाग्नेये ऋगग्नेर्मध्यमस्य तु | जराबोधेति विज्ञेया वैश्वदेव्युत्तमा नमः ||
text: Do thou put on' (vasisva hi: i. 26) are two (hymns) addressed to Agni (26, 27); but the stanza 'Thou that knowest lauds' (jarabodha: i. 27. 10) is to be recognized as (belonging) to the Middle Agni; the last (stanza) 'Obeisance' (namah: i. 27. 13) is addressed to the All-gods. vaisvadevyuttama namah 4, vaisvadevyudgamah, vaisvadevyanamadgamah 1, vaisvadevyuttamottama 1. r.

sanskrit_iast: parāścatasro yatreti indrolūkhalayo stutiḥ | manyete yāskakātthakyāv indrasyeti tu bhāguriḥ ||
meaning: पराश्चतस्रो यत्रेति इन्द्रोलूखलयो स्तुतिः | मन्येते यास्ककात्थक्याव् इन्द्रस्येति तु भागुरिः ||
text: The following four (stanzas), 'Where' (yatra: i. 28. 1-4), are (in) praise of Indra and the Mortar, (so) think Yaska a and Katthakya, but Bhaguri (thinks) of Indra (alone).

sanskrit_iast: yacciddhyūlūkhalasya dve dve pare musalasya tu | carmādhiṣavaṇīyaṃ vā somaṃ vāntyā praśaṃsati ||
meaning: यच्चिद्ध्यूलूखलस्य द्वे द्वे परे मुसलस्य तु | चर्माधिषवणीयं वा सोमं वान्त्या प्रशंसति ||
text: 'If indeed' (yac cid dhi: i. 28. 5) a are two (stanzas in praise) of the Mortar (5, 6), the two following (7, 8) are (in praise) of the Pestle also; the last (stanza) lauds the skin used in pressing (adhisavaniya) or Soma.

sanskrit_iast: aindra yacciddhi satyeti uttaraṃ cāśvinātṛcāt | āśvināduttaraḥ kasta uṣasyastṛca uttamaḥ ||
meaning: ऐन्द्र यच्चिद्धि सत्येति उत्तरं चाश्विनातृचात् | आश्विनादुत्तरः कस्त उषस्यस्तृच उत्तमः ||
text: 'What though, O True One' (yac cid dhi satya: i. 29) is addressed to Indra as well as the following (i. 30). After the 108 triplet Hither, O Asvins' (asvina: i. 30. 17-19), addressed to the Asvins, the next (uttara) triplet Who of thee' (kas te: 20-22), addressed to Dawn, is the last (triplet).

sanskrit_iast: stūyamānaḥ śaśvaditi prītastu manasā dadau | śunaḥśepāya divyaṃ tu rathaṃ sarvaṃ hiraṇmayam ||
meaning: स्तूयमानः शश्वदिति प्रीतस्तु मनसा ददौ | शुनःशेपाय दिव्यं तु रथं सर्वं हिरण्मयम् ||
text: Being praised (with the stanza) 'For ever' (sasvat: i. 30. 16), he (Indra) a rejoiced in mind gave to Sunahsepa (the seer) a celestial car all made of gold.

sanskrit_iast: āgneyaṃ yattvamaindre ca triścidityāśvinaṃ tataḥ | ṛte'rthavādaṃ karmaitad indrasyeti tu śaṃsati ||
meaning: आग्नेयं यत्त्वमैन्द्रे च त्रिश्चिदित्याश्विनं ततः | ऋतेऽर्थवादं कर्मैतद् इन्द्रस्येति तु शंसति ||
text: The (hymn) which (begins) Thou' (tvam: i. 31) is addressed to Agni; and (then come) two (32, 33) addressed to Indra. Then 'Even thrice' (tris cid: i. 34) is addressed to the Asvins; 'Of Indra' (indrasya: i. 32) lauds the action (of Indra) without (any) statement of an object (artha-vada). yatvam hrºfkr±rr 7, yattam, suktam r.

sanskrit_iast: pādo'gnaye hvayāmīti maitrāvaruṇa uttaraḥ | tṛtīyo rātrisaṃstāvaḥ sūktaṃ sāvitramucyate ||
meaning: पादोऽग्नये ह्वयामीति मैत्रावरुण उत्तरः | तृतीयो रात्रिसंस्तावः सूक्तं सावित्रमुच्यते ||
text: (In) 'I invoke' (hvayami: i. 35) one verse (19) is to Agni, the next (1) is addressed to Mitra-Varuna, the third (1) is (in) praise of Night, (while) the (whole) hymn is stated to be addressed to Savitr. i.

sanskrit_iast: pañcaitāni jagau dṛṣṭvā sūktānyāṅgiraso muni | hiraṇyastūpatāṃ prāpya sakhyaṃ cendreṇa śāśvatam ||
meaning: पञ्चैतानि जगौ दृष्ट्वा सूक्तान्याङ्गिरसो मुनि | हिरण्यस्तूपतां प्राप्य सख्यं चेन्द्रेण शाश्वतम् ||
text: These five hymns (31-35) a the sage, the son of Angiras, after he had seen them, sang, on gaining the position of Hiranyastupa and eternal friendship with Indra.

sanskrit_iast: āgneyaṃ preti marutāṃ krīḻaṃ trīṇi parāṇyataḥ | uttiṣṭha brāhmaṇaspatyaṃ yaṃ rakṣanti trayastṛcāḥ ||
meaning: आग्नेयं प्रेति मरुतां क्रीḻअं त्रीणि पराण्यतः | उत्तिष्ठ ब्राह्मणस्पत्यं यं रक्षन्ति त्रयस्तृचाः ||
text: Forth' (pra: i. 36) is addressed to Agni; the three (37-39) following this (beginning) 'Sporting' (krilam: i. 37) are to the Maruts. 'Stand up' (ut tistha: i. 40) is addressed to Brahmanaspati. 'Whom they protect' (yam raksanti: i. 41) is (composed of) three

sanskrit_iast: varuṇāryamamitrāṇāṃ madhyaṃ ādityadaivataḥ | pauṣṇaṃ saṃ pūṣanṣaḍraudryas tṛtīyā na tu kevalā ||
meaning: वरुणार्यममित्राणां मध्यं आदित्यदैवतः | पौष्णं सं पूषन्षड्रौद्र्यस् तृतीया न तु केवला ||
text: (the first, 1-3, and the third, 7-9, being addressed) to Varuna, Aryaman, and Mitra, (while) the middle one (4-6) has the Adityas for its divinities. Shorten, O Pusan' (sam pusan: i. 42) is addressed to Pusan. (Then come) six (stanzas) addressed to Rudra (i. 43. 1-6), the third, however, not exclusively.

sanskrit_iast: mitreṇa varuṇenātra viśvedevaiśca saṃstavaḥ | uktamatrarṣiṇā pūrvam ādeśāddaivataṃ vinā ||
meaning: मित्रेण वरुणेनात्र विश्वेदेवैश्च संस्तवः | उक्तमत्रर्षिणा पूर्वम् आदेशाद्दैवतं विना ||
text: There is here (i. 43. 3) praise (of Rudra) along with Mitra, Varuna, and the All-gods. B It has already been said before a by the seer b that without an authoritative statement (adesa) the divinity

sanskrit_iast: jñātuṃ na śakyate liṅgāt tathāpi kvaciducyate | ādityā vasavo rudrās tvamagna iti saṃstutāḥ ||
meaning: ज्ञातुं न शक्यते लिङ्गात् तथापि क्वचिदुच्यते | आदित्या वसवो रुद्रास् त्वमग्न इति संस्तुताः ||

sanskrit_iast: tisraḥ saumyo'gna āgneye pragāthenāśvinau stutau | sahoṣasā liṅgabhājā ayaṃ soma sudānavaḥ ||
meaning: तिस्रः सौम्योऽग्न आग्नेये प्रगाथेनाश्विनौ स्तुतौ | सहोषसा लिङ्गभाजा अयं सोम सुदानवः ||
text: (Then come) three (stanzas) addressed to Soma (i. 43. 7-9). 'O Agni' (agne: i. 44. 1) are two (hymns) addressed to Agni (44, 45). With Pragatha couplet a the Asvins are (here) b praised with Dawn who bears her characteristic mark (linga-bhaj). 'Here is Soma, O bounteous ones' (ayam somah sudanavah: i. 45. 10ºd)

sanskrit_iast: ardharco devadevasya eṣo ityāśvine pare | ādityaṃ manyate yāsko haviṣeti saha stutam ||
meaning: अर्धर्चो देवदेवस्य एषो इत्याश्विने परे | आदित्यं मन्यते यास्को हविषेति सह स्तुतम् ||

sanskrit_iast: sahauṣase tataḥ sauryam udu tyamiti saṃstutaḥ | dyubhaktiryena varuṇo rogaghnastṛca uttamaḥ ||
meaning: सहौषसे ततः सौर्यम् उदु त्यमिति संस्तुतः | द्युभक्तिर्येन वरुणो रोगघ्नस्तृच उत्तमः ||
text: Together with' (saha: i. 48. 1) are two (hymns) addressed to Dawn (48, 49); then 'Upward him' (ud u tyam: i. 50) is addressed to Surya: (in) 'Wherewith' (yena: i. 50. 6) Varuna a connected with Heaven (dyubhakti) is praised; the last triplet (50. 11-13) is destructive of disease (rogaghna).

sanskrit_iast: rogāpanuttirādyābhyām udyannisyuttame tṛce | ardharce tu dviṣaddveṣaḥ aindraḥ savyaḥ śatarciṣu ||
meaning: रोगापनुत्तिराद्याभ्याम् उद्यन्निस्युत्तमे तृचे | अर्धर्चे तु द्विषद्द्वेषः ऐन्द्रः सव्यः शतर्चिषु ||
text: With the first two (stanzas) in the last triplet (beginning) 'Rising' (udyan: i. 50. 11, 12) there is driving away of disease, while in a hemistich (of the last stanza) there is hostility to foes. Among the Satarcins is Savyad who is a form of Indra (aindra).

sanskrit_iast: svayamindrasamaṃ putram icchato'ṅgiraso muneḥ | vajryeva savyo bhūtvarṣer yogitvātputratāṃ gataḥ ||
meaning: स्वयमिन्द्रसमं पुत्रम् इच्छतोऽङ्गिरसो मुनेः | वज्र्येव सव्यो भूत्वर्षेर् योगित्वात्पुत्रतां गतः ||
text: Of the sage Angiras who wished for a son like Indra, the Bolt-bearer himself became the sona, having assumed the form of Savya in consequence of the seer's asceticism.

sanskrit_iast: prathame maṇḍale jñeyā ṛṣayastu śatarcinaḥ | kṣudrasūktamahāsūktā antye madhyeṣu madhyamāḥ ||
meaning: प्रथमे मण्डले ज्ञेया ऋषयस्तु शतर्चिनः | क्षुद्रसूक्तमहासूक्ता अन्त्ये मध्येषु मध्यमाः ||
text: Now the seers in the first book are to be known as Satarcins; in the last, as seers of short hymns and of long hymns; in the middle ones, as middlemen (madhyama).

sanskrit_iast: navakaṃ jātavedasyaṃ nan cid yattu vayā iti | vaiśvānarīyaṃ tatsūktaṃ vahnimāgneyamuttaram ||
meaning: नवकं जातवेदस्यं नन् चिद् यत्तु वया इति | वैश्वानरीयं तत्सूक्तं वह्निमाग्नेयमुत्तरम् ||
text: 'Now indeed' (nu cit: i. 58), containing nine stanzas, is addressed to Jatavedas; while the hymn which (begins) 'Branches' (vayah i. 59) is addressed to Vaisvanara; the following one, 'Bearer' (vahnim: i. 60), is addressed to Agni. nu

sanskrit_iast: aindrāṇyasmai tatastrīṇi vṛṣṇo śardhāya māratam | āgneyāni tu paśveti navaśaśvaddhi vāmiti ||
meaning: ऐन्द्राण्यस्मै ततस्त्रीणि वृष्णो शर्धाय मारतम् | आग्नेयानि तु पश्वेति नवशश्वद्धि वामिति ||
text: Then (come) three (61-63), 'To him' (asmai: i. 61), addressed to Indra; For the manly host' (vrsne sardhaya: i. 64) is addressed to the Maruts; 'With a cow' (pasva: i. 65) is (the first of) nine hymns (65-73) addressed to Agni; 'Ever indeed of you' (sasvad dhi vam)

sanskrit_iast: daśāśvinānīmānīti indrāvaruṇayo stutiḥ | sauparṇeyāstu yāḥ kāścinnipātastutiṣu stutāḥ ||
meaning: दशाश्विनानीमानीति इन्द्रावरुणयो स्तुतिः | सौपर्णेयास्तु याः काश्चिन्निपातस्तुतिषु स्तुताः ||

sanskrit_iast: upaprayantaḥ sūktāni āgneyānyuttarāṇi ṣaṭ | hiraṇyakeśo rajasaḥ tṛco'gnermadhyamasya tu ||
meaning: उपप्रयन्तः सूक्तानि आग्नेयान्युत्तराणि षट् | हिरण्यकेशो रजसः तृचोऽग्नेर्मध्यमस्य तु ||
text: The following six hymns (74-79), 'Going forth' (upaprayantah: i. 74. 1), are addressed to Agni ; but the triplet 'With golden locks, of air' (hiranyakeso rajasah: i. 79. 1-3) is (addressed) to the middle Agni.

sanskrit_iast: ittheti pañca tvaindrāṇi yāmityasyāṃ nipātitāḥ | dadhyaṅ manuratharvā ca mārutāni pra ye tataḥ ||
meaning: इत्थेति पञ्च त्वैन्द्राणि यामित्यस्यां निपातिताः | दध्यङ् मनुरथर्वा च मारुतानि प्र ये ततः ||
text: Now 'Thus' (ittha: i. 80. 1) are five (80-84) addressed to Indra; in the (stanza) Whatever' (yam: i. 80. 16) Dadhyanc, Manu, and Atharvan are incidentally mentioned. Then They who forth' (pra ye: (pra ye: i. 85. 1) are addressed to the Maruts, II.

sanskrit_iast: catvāryā no vaiśvadeve dve devānāṃ stutimate | ā no bhadrāśca devānāṃ bhadraṃ yāvacchataṃ punaḥ ||
meaning: चत्वार्या नो वैश्वदेवे द्वे देवानां स्तुतिमते | आ नो भद्राश्च देवानां भद्रं यावच्छतं पुनः ||

sanskrit_iast: madhu vātāstṛce tasmin paramaṃ madhvapīṣyate | aditirdyauriti tvasyāṃ vibhūtiḥ kathitāditeḥ ||
meaning: मधु वातास्तृचे तस्मिन् परमं मध्वपीष्यते | अदितिर्द्यौरिति त्वस्यां विभूतिः कथितादितेः ||
text: In the triplet 'The winds waft mead' (madhu vatah: i. 90. 6) the supreme (parama) mead is also (api) a desired; but in the (stanza) Aditi is Heaven' (aditir dyauh: i. 89. 10) the majesty of Aditi is told.

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ saumyamauṣasam etā u tyāstṛco'śvinoḥ | aśvitāgneḥ sasomasya agnīṣomāviti stutiḥ ||
meaning: त्वं सौम्यमौषसम् एता उ त्यास्तृचोऽश्विनोः | अश्विताग्नेः ससोमस्य अग्नीषोमाविति स्तुतिः ||
text: 'Thou, Soma' (tvam soma: i. 91) is addressed to Soma; These Dawns' (eta u tyah: i. 92) is addressed to Dawn; the triplet O Asvins' (asvina: i. 92. 16-18), to the Asvins. Agni and Soma' (agnisomau: i. 93) is (in) praise of Agni associated with Soma. i.

sanskrit_iast: gotamādauśijaḥ kutsaḥ parucchepādṛṣeḥ paraḥ | kutsaddīrghatamāḥ śaśvat te dve evamadhīyate ||
meaning: गोतमादौशिजः कुत्सः परुच्छेपादृषेः परः | कुत्सद्दीर्घतमाः शश्वत् ते द्वे एवमधीयते ||
text: After Gotama (74-93) the son of Usij (Kaksivat comes: 116-126); after the seer Paruchepa (127-139) follows Kutsa (94-115); after Kutsa, Dirghatamasa (140-164): always (sasvat) these twob (sets respectively); in this order (evam) is read (the text of the Rg-veda).

sanskrit_iast: imaṃ kutsa āṅgiraso dadarśa jātavedasyaṃ jagāda ṣoḻaśarcam | pūrvo devā ityṛco devadevās trayaḥ pādā uttamāyāstato'rdham ||
meaning: इमं कुत्स आङ्गिरसो ददर्श जातवेदस्यं जगाद षोḻअशर्चम् | पूर्वो देवा इत्यृचो देवदेवास् त्रयः पादा उत्तमायास्ततोऽर्धम् ||
text: Kutsa, son of Angiras, saw 'This' (imam: i. 94): he uttered (this hymn) containing sixteen stanzas (and) addressed to Jatavedas. A Three verses (8 abc) of the stanza Foremost, O Gods' (purvo devah: i. 94. 8) have the gods as their deities; then half of the last (stanza: i. 94. 16)

sanskrit_iast: tasyaiva vā yasya tatpūrvasūktaṃ mitrā- dibhyo vātra ṣaḍbhyaḥ prakṛtābhyaḥ | antyo'rdharcastu vā ṣaṇṇāṃ stutānāṃ pūrvo devāḥ pādastu tribhi stutāḥ ||
meaning: तस्यैव वा यस्य तत्पूर्वसूक्तं मित्रा- दिभ्यो वात्र षड्भ्यः प्रकृताभ्यः | अन्त्योऽर्धर्चस्तु वा षण्णां स्तुतानां पूर्वो देवाः पादस्तु त्रिभि स्तुताः ||

sanskrit_iast: bharadvāje gṛtsamade vasiṣṭhe nodhasyagastye vimade nabhāke | kutse nodarkā bahudaivateṣu tathā dvideveṣu samānadharmiṇaḥ ||
meaning: भरद्वाजे गृत्समदे वसिष्ठे नोधस्यगस्त्ये विमदे नभाके | कुत्से नोदर्का बहुदैवतेषु तथा द्विदेवेषु समानधर्मिणः ||

sanskrit_iast: dve virūpe sūktamauṣasāyāgnaye sa pratnatheti draviṇodase'gnaye | vaiśvānarasyeti vaiśvānarīyam asmātpūrvaṃ śucaye'gnaye punaḥ ||
meaning: द्वे विरूपे सूक्तमौषसायाग्नये स प्रत्नथेति द्रविणोदसेऽग्नये | वैश्वानरस्येति वैश्वानरीयम् अस्मात्पूर्वं शुचयेऽग्नये पुनः ||
text: Two unlike' (dve virupe: i. 95) is a hymn to Agni Ausasa, 'He in the ancient way' (sa pratnatha: i. 96) is to Agni Dravinodas, 'Of Vaisvanara' (vaisvanarasya: i. 98) is addressed to Vaisvanara; but the one before this (i. 97) is to Agni Suci.

sanskrit_iast: jātavedasyaṃ sūktasahasrameka aindrātpūrvaṃ kaśyapārṣaṃ vadanti | jātavedase sūktamādyaṃ tu teṣām ekabhūyastvaṃ manyate śākapūṇiḥ ||
meaning: जातवेदस्यं सूक्तसहस्रमेक ऐन्द्रात्पूर्वं कश्यपार्षं वदन्ति | जातवेदसे सूक्तमाद्यं तु तेषाम् एकभूयस्त्वं मन्यते शाकपूणिः ||
text: Some say that the thousand hymns addressed to Jatavedas (which come) before (the hymn) addressed to Indra (i. 100) have Kasyapa as their seera: the first hymn of these is 'For Jatavedas' (jatavedase: i. 99). Sakapuni thinks that they increase by one (in the number of their stanzas).

sanskrit_iast: sa yo vṛṣaindrāṇi pañca vaiśvadevāni candramāḥ | trīṇyaindrāgne ya indrāgnī tatamityārbhave pare ||
meaning: स यो वृषैन्द्राणि पञ्च वैश्वदेवानि चन्द्रमाः | त्रीण्यैन्द्राग्ने य इन्द्राग्नी ततमित्यार्भवे परे ||
text: The mighty one who' (sa yo vrsa: i. 100) is (the first of) five (hymns) addressed to Indra (100-104); there are (then) three (105-107) addressed to the All-gods, (beginning) 'The Moon' (candramas: i. 105. 1). 'That which, O Indra-Agni' (ya indragni: i. 108) is (the first of) two addressed to Indra-Agni (108, 109); the two following (110, 111) 'I wrought' (tatam: i. 110. 1) are addressed to the Rbhus.

sanskrit_iast: tritaṃ gāstvanugacchantaṃ krūrā sālāvṛkīsutāḥ | kūpe prakṣipya gāḥ sarvās tata evāpajahrire ||
meaning: त्रितं गास्त्वनुगच्छन्तं क्रूरा सालावृकीसुताः | कूपे प्रक्षिप्य गाः सर्वास् तत एवापजह्रिरे ||
text: The cruel sons of the she-wolf (salavrki) a having cast Trita, who was following the cows, into a well, carried off all the cows from thence.

sanskrit_iast: sa tatra suṣuve somaṃ mantravinmantravittamaḥ | devāṃścāvāhayatsarvāṃs tacchuśrāva bṛhaspatiḥ ||
meaning: स तत्र सुषुवे सोमं मन्त्रविन्मन्त्रवित्तमः | देवांश्चावाहयत्सर्वांस् तच्छुश्राव बृहस्पतिः ||
text: He, the best knower of formulas among all knowers of such, pressed Soma there and summoned all the gods: Brhaspati heard that (call). sa

sanskrit_iast: āgacchato'tha tāndṛṣṭvā kva vasatyasya tattvataḥ | sarvadṛktvaṃ ca varuṇasyāryamṇaścetyupālabhat ||
meaning: आगच्छतोऽथ तान्दृष्ट्वा क्व वसत्यस्य तत्त्वतः | सर्वदृक्त्वं च वरुणस्यार्यम्णश्चेत्युपालभत् ||
text: Now on seeing them coming, he reproached (them), saying, 'Where, indeed, abides, the all-seeing power (sarvadrktva) of this Varuna and of Aryaman?

sanskrit_iast: kūpeṣṭakābhirvraṇitāny saṅgānyevābhayanmama | dṛṣṭvā sarvānahaṃ staumi yadyapyeko na paśyati ||
meaning: कूपेष्टकाभिर्व्रणितान्य् सङ्गान्येवाभयन्मम | दृष्ट्वा सर्वानहं स्तौमि यद्यप्येको न पश्यति ||
text: 'My limbs were wounded by the bricks of the well. Having seen all (the gods) I praise (them), even though not one (of them) sees (me).'

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspatipracoditā viśvedevagaṇāstrayaḥ | jagmustritasya taṃ yajñaṃ bhāgāṃśca jagṛhuḥ saha ||
meaning: बृहस्पतिप्रचोदिता विश्वेदेवगणास्त्रयः | जग्मुस्त्रितस्य तं यज्ञं भागांश्च जगृहुः सह ||
text: The three troops a of the All-gods, urged on by Brhaspati, went to that sacrifice of Trita and took shares of it together.

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspatistritasyaitaj jñānaṃ vijñānameva ca | tṛcenāntyena sūktasya jagādarṣirasāviti ||
meaning: बृहस्पतिस्त्रितस्यैतज् ज्ञानं विज्ञानमेव च | तृचेनान्त्येन सूक्तस्य जगादर्षिरसाविति ||
text: As a seer Brhaspati declared the knowledge and discernment of Trita here displayed (etat) with the last triplet (i. 105. 16-18)a of the hymn (beginning) 'That' (asau: i. 105. 16).

sanskrit_iast: dyāvāpṛthivyorīḻeti āgneyaḥ pāda uttaraḥ | āśvinaḥ sūktaśeṣaḥ syāda idaṃ rātryuṣaso stutiḥ ||
meaning: द्यावापृथिव्योरीḻएति आग्नेयः पाद उत्तरः | आश्विनः सूक्तशेषः स्याद इदं रात्र्युषसो स्तुतिः ||
text: (The verse) 'I praise' (ile: i. 112. 1) is to Heaven and Earth, the next verse (1) is addressed to Agni ; the remainder of the hymn (112. 1 cd-25) should be (regarded as) addressed to the Asvinsa. 'This' (idam: i. 113) is (in) praise of Night and Dawn. I

sanskrit_iast: imā raudraṃ paraṃ sauryaṃ citraṃ paścāśvinānyataḥ | nāsatyābhyāmiti tvantye antyā duḥsvapnanāśino ||
meaning: इमा रौद्रं परं सौर्यं चित्रं पश्चाश्विनान्यतः | नासत्याभ्यामिति त्वन्त्ये अन्त्या दुःस्वप्ननाशिनो ||
text: 'These' (imah: i. 114) is addressed to Rudra; the next, 'The brilliant' (citram: i. 115), is addressed to the Sun. Then 120 (come) five (i. 116-120) addressed to the Asvins (beginning) 'For the Nasatyas' (nasatyabhyam: i. 116. 1): the last (stanza) in the last (hymn i. 120. 12) is destructive of evil dreams.

sanskrit_iast: aindraṃ kadvaiśvadevaṃ ca prauṣase pṛthuruttare | ṛṣirdānaṃ ca bhāvyasya prātarityatra śaṃsati ||
meaning: ऐन्द्रं कद्वैश्वदेवं च प्रौषसे पृथुरुत्तरे | ऋषिर्दानं च भाव्यस्य प्रातरित्यत्र शंसति ||
text: When?' (kad: i. 121) is addressed to Indra, and 'Forth' (pra: i. 122) is addressed to the All-gods. The two (123, 124) next (beginning) 'Broad' (prthuh: i. 123. 1) are addressed to Dawn (ausase). In 'At morn' (pratah: i. 125) the seer lauds the gift of Bhavyaa.

sanskrit_iast: kākṣīvataṃ kadittheti yadaindramupadiśyate | parokṣaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tat pradiṣṭaṃ svarasāmasu ||
meaning: काक्षीवतं कदित्थेति यदैन्द्रमुपदिश्यते | परोक्षं वैश्वदेवं तत् प्रदिष्टं स्वरसामसु ||
text: 'When, indeed?' (kad ittha: i. 121), a hymn of Kaksivat which is traditionally held to be addressed to Indra, is indicated as indirectly addressed (paroksa) to the All-gods in the Svarasamansa.

sanskrit_iast: adhigamya gurorvidyāṃ gacchansvanilayaṃ kila | kakṣīvānadhvani śrāntaḥ suṣvāpāraṇyagocaraḥ ||
meaning: अधिगम्य गुरोर्विद्यां गच्छन्स्वनिलयं किल | कक्षीवानध्वनि श्रान्तः सुष्वापारण्यगोचरः ||
text: Having acquired knowledge from his spiritual teacher (and) going home, as we are told (kila), Kaksivat fatigued on the way fell asleep within the forest.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ rājā svanayo nāma bhāvayavyasuto vrajan | krīḍārthaṃ sānugo'paśyat sabhāryaḥ sapurohitaḥ ||
meaning: तं राजा स्वनयो नाम भावयव्यसुतो व्रजन् | क्रीडार्थं सानुगोऽपश्यत् सभार्यः सपुरोहितः ||
text: Him a king, Svanaya by name, the son of Bhavayavya, saw as he went along to amuse himself, accompanied by his retinue, his wife, and his domestic priest. bhavayavyasuto hm`rn (d), bhavayavyastuto, bhavayavyastato fkr'n (ab). The reading °suto is supported by Sayana (on Rg-veda i. 125. 1, where the story of Kaksivat is told), who calls Svanaya bhavayavyasya putrah | . - The unanimity of the MSS. in writing kridartham has caused a lapse from consistency, which requires in the text.

sanskrit_iast: athainaṃ rūpasaṃpannaṃ dṛṣṭvā devasutopamam | kanyādāne matiṃ cakre varṇagotrāvirodhataḥ ||
meaning: अथैनं रूपसंपन्नं दृष्ट्वा देवसुतोपमम् | कन्यादाने मतिं चक्रे वर्णगोत्राविरोधतः ||
text: Then on seeing him endowed with beauty (and) resembling the son of a god, he thought of bestowing his daughter (on him), if there were no objection on the score of caste and family.

sanskrit_iast: saṃbodhyainaṃ sa papraccha varṇagotrādikaṃ tataḥ | rājannāṅgiraso'smīti kumāraḥ pratyuvāca tam ||
meaning: संबोध्यैनं स पप्रच्छ वर्णगोत्रादिकं ततः | राजन्नाङ्गिरसोऽस्मीति कुमारः प्रत्युवाच तम् ||
text: Then after wakening him he inquired as to his caste, family, and so forth. The youth replied to him saying, 'O king, I am of the race of Angiras; cd:

sanskrit_iast: putro'haṃ dīrghatamasa aucathyasya ṛṣernṛpa | athāsmai sa dadau kanyā daśābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ ||
meaning: पुत्रोऽहं दीर्घतमस औचथ्यस्य ऋषेर्नृप | अथास्मै स ददौ कन्या दशाभरणभूषिताः ||
text: A similar distinction between dhana and kupya is found in Manu vii. 96. There is no reference to these, nor to sheep and goats, in the text of the hymn.

sanskrit_iast: tāvataśca rathāñchyāvān vīḍvaṅgānvai caturyujaḥ | vadhūnāṃ vāhanārthāya dhanakupyamajāvikam ||
meaning: तावतश्च रथाञ्छ्यावान् वीड्वङ्गान्वै चतुर्युजः | वधूनां वाहनार्थाय धनकुप्यमजाविकम् ||

sanskrit_iast: niṣkāṇāṃ vṛṣabhāṇāṃ ca śataṃ śatamadātpunaḥ | etaduttarasūktena śatamityādinoditam ||
meaning: निष्काणां वृषभाणां च शतं शतमदात्पुनः | एतदुत्तरसूक्तेन शतमित्यादिनोदितम् ||
text: Further he gave (him) a hundred necklets and a hundred bulls. This is told in the next hymn with (the stanza) A hundred' (satam: i. 126. 2) and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: śatamaśvāñchataṃ niṣkān rathāndaśa vadhūmataḥ | caturyujo gavāṃ caiva sahasraṃ ṣaṣṭhyupādhikam ||
meaning: शतमश्वाञ्छतं निष्कान् रथान्दश वधूमतः | चतुर्युजो गवां चैव सहस्रं षष्ठ्युपाधिकम् ||
text: A hundred horses, a hundred necklets, ten chariots with maidens, (steeds) going in teams of four, and a thousand and sixty cows

sanskrit_iast: svanayādbhāvayavyādyaḥ kakṣīvānpratyapadyata | pratigṛhya ca tuṣṭāva prātaḥ pitre śaśaṃsa ca ||
meaning: स्वनयाद्भावयव्याद्यः कक्षीवान्प्रत्यपद्यत | प्रतिगृह्य च तुष्टाव प्रातः पित्रे शशंस च ||
text: Kaksivat, who obtained (all this) from Svanaya Bhavayavya, both praised (him) after receiving (it) and recited (the hymn) 'At morn' (pratah: i. 125) to his father. i.

sanskrit_iast: phalapradarśanaṃ tasya kriyate prāyaśastviha | dvitīyāṃ tu pitāpaśyat sugurityādikāmṛcam ||
meaning: फलप्रदर्शनं तस्य क्रियते प्रायशस्त्विह | द्वितीयां तु पितापश्यत् सुगुरित्यादिकामृचम् ||
text: Now here (in 125) the rewards (of liberality) are for the most part set forth to him. The father, however, saw the second (stanza), which begins Possessed of many kine' (suguh: 125. 2). The three slokas 151-153 are found in

sanskrit_iast: kākṣīvataṃ sarvamiti bhagavānāha śaunakaḥ | eṣā tu dairghatamasī sānuliṅgā kathaṃ bhavet ||
meaning: काक्षीवतं सर्वमिति भगवानाह शौनकः | एषा तु दैर्घतमसी सानुलिङ्गा कथं भवेत् ||
text: The revered Saunaka says that the whole (hymn) is Kaksivat's. But as to this (stanza), how could it, according to the indications (it contains), have been seen by

sanskrit_iast: ucyate prātarityukte sūnordānena harṣitaḥ | rājñaścāśiṣamāhātha sugurityādinā kila ||
meaning: उच्यते प्रातरित्युक्ते सूनोर्दानेन हर्षितः | राज्ञश्चाशिषमाहाथ सुगुरित्यादिना किल ||
text: The answer is, that when 'At morn' (pratah: i. 125. 1) had been uttered (by Kaksivat), he (Dirghatamas) was delighted by the gift to his son, and then uttered a prayer for the king with (the stanza) 'Possessed of many kine' (suguh: i. 125. 2).

sanskrit_iast: karmāṇi yābhiḥ kathitāni rājñāṃ dānāni coccāvacamadhyamāni | nārāśaṃsīrityṛcastāḥ pratīyād yābhi stutirdāśatayīṣu rājñām ||
meaning: कर्माणि याभिः कथितानि राज्ञां दानानि चोच्चावचमध्यमानि | नाराशंसीरित्यृचस्ताः प्रतीयाद् याभि स्तुतिर्दाशतयीषु राज्ञाम् ||
text: The stanzas in which the deeds of kings and their gifts, great, small, and middling, are told, should be understood to be called Laudations of Men' (narasamsi), as the praise of kings (is expressed) by them in the ten books (of the Rg-veda).

sanskrit_iast: pañcāmandānbhāvayavyasya gītā jāyāpatyoḥ saṃpravādo dvṛcena | saṃpravādaṃ romaśayendrarājñora ete ṛcau manyate śākapūṇiḥ ||
meaning: पञ्चामन्दान्भावयव्यस्य गीता जायापत्योः संप्रवादो द्वृचेन | संप्रवादं रोमशयेन्द्रराज्ञोर एते ऋचौ मन्यते शाकपूणिः ||
text: The five (stanzas) 'Lively' (amandan : 1. 126. 1-5) are a song (in praise) of Bhavayavya. With a couplet (6, 7) there is a conversation of a husband and wife. Sakapuni thinks these two stanzas are a conversation of Indra and the king with Romasa.

sanskrit_iast: indre jāyāpatyoścetihāsaṃ dvṛce'sminmanyate śākaṭāyanaḥ | prādātsutāṃ romaśāṃ nāma nāmnā bṛhaspatirbhāvayavyāya rājño ||
meaning: इन्द्रे जायापत्योश्चेतिहासं द्वृचेऽस्मिन्मन्यते शाकटायनः | प्रादात्सुतां रोमशां नाम नाम्ना बृहस्पतिर्भावयव्याय राज्ञो ||
text: Sakatayana thinks that in this couplet there is a story of a husband and wife (in connexion) with Indra. Brhaspati gave his daughter, Romasa by name, to king Bhavayavya. r.

sanskrit_iast: tatastamarthaṃ harivānviditvā priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ svanayaṃ didṛkṣuḥ | abhyājagāmāśu śacīsahāyaḥ prītyārcayattaṃ vidhinaiva rājā ||
meaning: ततस्तमर्थं हरिवान्विदित्वा प्रियं सखायं स्वनयं दिदृक्षुः | अभ्याजगामाशु शचीसहायः प्रीत्यार्चयत्तं विधिनैव राजा ||
text: Then the Lord of Bays, the Companion of Saci (Indra) becoming aware of that affair, (and) desirous of seeing his dear friend Svanaya, quickly went to him. him with due ceremony. The king joyfully

sanskrit_iast: abhyājagāmāṅgirasī ca tatra hṛṣṭā tayoḥ sā caraṇau vavande | indraḥ sakhitvādatha tāmuvāca romāṇi te santi na santi rājñi ||
meaning: अभ्याजगामाङ्गिरसी च तत्र हृष्टा तयोः सा चरणौ ववन्दे | इन्द्रः सखित्वादथ तामुवाच रोमाणि ते सन्ति न सन्ति राज्ञि ||
text: And the daughter of the Angiras (Brhaspati) came there: rejoicing she adored their feet. Indra then in a friendly way said to her, 'Have you hair or have you not, O Queen?'

sanskrit_iast: sā bālabhāvādatha taṃ jagāda upopa me śakra parāmṛśeti | tāṃ pūrvayā sāntvya nṛpaḥ prahṛṣṭo anvavrajatsātha patiṃ pativratāṃ ||
meaning: सा बालभावादथ तं जगाद उपोप मे शक्र परामृशेति | तां पूर्वया सान्त्व्य नृपः प्रहृष्टो अन्वव्रजत्साथ पतिं पतिव्रतां ||
text: She in a childlike way then addressed him, 'Feel me closely (upopa me: i. 126. 7), Mighty One'a. The king having soothed her with the previous (stanza: i. 126. 6), rejoiced. She then followed her husband as a devoted wife. r.

sanskrit_iast: athāgneye agnimityuttare yaṃ pañcaindrāṇi pra tadaindavyṛgatra | śaṃ tamindrāparvatau saha stutau tvindraṃ mena iha yāskaḥ pradhānam ||
meaning: अथाग्नेये अग्निमित्युत्तरे यं पञ्चैन्द्राणि प्र तदैन्दव्यृगत्र | शं तमिन्द्रापर्वतौ सह स्तुतौ त्विन्द्रं मेन इह यास्कः प्रधानम् ||
text: Next follow two hymns (127, 128) addressed to Agni (beginning) 'Agni' (agnim: i. 127). There are (then) five (129- 133) addressed to Indra (beginning) Which' (yam: i. 129). Here the stanza 'Forth this' (pra tad: i. 129. 6) is addressed to Indu, while Indra-Parvata are praised together (in) 'Ye him' (yuvam tam: i. 132. 6). Yaska here considered Indra to be predominant.

sanskrit_iast: ṛkṣu stutaḥ parvatavaddhi vajro dvivatstutau cendramāhuḥ pradhānam | ā tvā vāyonava pañcendravāyvor ekā vāyoruttaraṃ dvipradhānam ||
meaning: ऋक्षु स्तुतः पर्वतवद्धि वज्रो द्विवत्स्तुतौ चेन्द्रमाहुः प्रधानम् | आ त्वा वायोनव पञ्चेन्द्रवाय्वोर् एका वायोरुत्तरं द्विप्रधानम् ||
text: For in (certain) stanzas (Indra's) bolt is praised as Parvata, and when there is praise (of the two) in the dual (dvivat-stutau) they say that Indra is predominant. (Beginning with) 'Hither thee' (a tva: i. 134. 1) there are nine (stanzas: i. 134. 1-6, 135. 1-3) to Vayu, (then) five (i. 135. 4-8) to Indra-Vayu, (then) one (i. 135. 9) to Vayu. The next (hymn: i. 136) has two predominant (deities).

sanskrit_iast: tatra pañca varuṇamitradevā divādibhyaḥ kathitābhyaḥ pare dve | dve dve pade saṃstute rodasī ca devāścārdharcena vibhaktamanyat ||
meaning: तत्र पञ्च वरुणमित्रदेवा दिवादिभ्यः कथिताभ्यः परे द्वे | द्वे द्वे पदे संस्तुते रोदसी च देवाश्चार्धर्चेन विभक्तमन्यत् ||
text: There five (stanzas: i. 136. 1-5) have Varuna and Mitra for their gods; the following two (i. 136. 6, 7) are (addressed) to the (deities) mentioned, Dyaus and the rest. Couples (of deities: dve dve), including the Two Worlds (rodasi), are praised together (samstute), (each) in a verse (pada), and the gods (are praised) with a hemistich (7); the rest (7 cd) is distributed (in praise). C r.

sanskrit_iast: maitrāvaruṇaṃ suṣumeti sūktaṃ prapra pauṣṇaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīyam | astu śrauṣaḍ vaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ syādbahudevateṣu ||
meaning: मैत्रावरुणं सुषुमेति सूक्तं प्रप्र पौष्णं वैश्वदेवं तृतीयम् | अस्तु श्रौषड् वैश्वदेवं तृतीयं वैश्वदेवं स्याद्बहुदेवतेषु ||
text: The hymn 'We have pressed' (i. 137) is addressed to MitraVaruna. Forth, forth' (pra-pra: i. 138) is addressed to Pusan, the third (i. 139) is addressed to the All-gods. 'Let it be heard' (astu srausat: i. 139) is the third hymn addressed to the All-gods. A hymn to the All-gods may be (included) among those which contain many deities.

sanskrit_iast: bahuśastu vaiśvadeveṣu santyṛcaḥ pādārdharcā dvaipadāstraipadāśca | dvipradhānā api caikapradhānā bahupradhānā api vaiśvadevāḥ ||
meaning: बहुशस्तु वैश्वदेवेषु सन्त्यृचः पादार्धर्चा द्वैपदास्त्रैपदाश्च | द्विप्रधाना अपि चैकप्रधाना बहुप्रधाना अपि वैश्वदेवाः ||
text: There are variously (bahusah), in (hymns) addressed to the All-gods, stanzas, verses, hemistichsa, stanzas with two verses (dvaipadah) or with three (traipadah): (such) Vaisvadeva (formulas) have two predominant (deities) or one predominant (deity) or many predominant (deities).

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvadevī maitrāvaruṇī dvitīyā tisro'śvibhyāṃ tata aindrī tato'gneḥ | mārutyekā tata aindrāgnyanantarā bārhaspatyā cottamā stauti devān ||
meaning: वैश्वदेवी मैत्रावरुणी द्वितीया तिस्रोऽश्विभ्यां तत ऐन्द्री ततोऽग्नेः | मारुत्येका तत ऐन्द्राग्न्यनन्तरा बार्हस्पत्या चोत्तमा स्तौति देवान् ||
text: There is (one: i. 139. 1) addressed to the All-gods, the second (2) is addressed to Mitra -Varuna; three (3-5) are to the Asvins, then (one) is addressed to Indra (6), then (one) to Agni (7), one is addressed to the Maruts (8), then (one) is addressed to Indra-Agni (9); and the next is addressed to Brhaspati (10); the last (stanza) praises the gods (11).

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣīnṛṣirvā stauti dadhyaṅha me'syām ātmānaṃ vā teṣu śaṃsansvajanma | tasmādasyāṃ vipravadanti kecid indrāgnī tasyāṃ tu nipātabhājau ||
meaning: ऋषीनृषिर्वा स्तौति दध्यङ्ह मेऽस्याम् आत्मानं वा तेषु शंसन्स्वजन्म | तस्मादस्यां विप्रवदन्ति केचिद् इन्द्राग्नी तस्यां तु निपातभाजौ ||
text: The seer in the (stanza) 'Dadhyanc of me' (dadhyan ha me: i. 139. 9) praises either the (ancient) seers or himself a by 128 some proclaiming his own origin among them. For this reason b disagree in regard to this (stanza, saying), that Indra-Agni are at the same time (tu) incidentally praised (nipata-bhaj) in it.

sanskrit_iast: dvāvucathyabṛhaspatī ṛṣiputrau babhūvatuḥ | āsīducathyabhāryā tu mamatā nāma bhārgavī ||
meaning: द्वावुचथ्यबृहस्पती ऋषिपुत्रौ बभूवतुः | आसीदुचथ्यभार्या तु ममता नाम भार्गवी ||
text: There were (once) two seers' sons, Ucathya and Brhaspati. Now Ucathya's wife was Mamata by name, of the race of Bhrgu.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ kanīyānbṛhaspatir maithunāyopacakrame | śukrasyotsargakāle tu garbhastaṃ pratyabhāṣata ||
meaning: तां कनीयान्बृहस्पतिर् मैथुनायोपचक्रमे | शुक्रस्योत्सर्गकाले तु गर्भस्तं प्रत्यभाषत ||
text: Brhaspati, the younger (of the two), approached her for sexual intercourse. Now at the time of impregnation the embryo addressed him:

sanskrit_iast: ihāsmi pūrvasaṃbhūto na kāryaḥ śukrasaṃkaraḥ | tacchrukrapratiṣedhaṃ tu na mamarṣa bṛhaspatiḥ ||
meaning: इहास्मि पूर्वसंभूतो न कार्यः शुक्रसंकरः | तच्छ्रुक्रप्रतिषेधं तु न ममर्ष बृहस्पतिः ||
text: 'Here am I previously engendered; you must not cause a commingling of seed.' Brhaspati, however, could not brook this remonstrance about the seed.

sanskrit_iast: sa vyājahāra taṃ garbhaṃ tamaste dīrghamastviti | sa ca dīrghatamā nāma babhūvarṣirucathyajaḥ ||
meaning: स व्याजहार तं गर्भं तमस्ते दीर्घमस्त्विति | स च दीर्घतमा नाम बभूवर्षिरुचथ्यजः ||
text: (So) he addressed the embryo: 'Long darkness shall be your lot.' And (hence) the seer, Ucathya's son, was born with the name Dirghatamas (Long Darkness). tam

sanskrit_iast: sa jāto'bhyatapaddevān akasmādandhatāṃ gataḥ | dadurdevāstu tannetre tato'nandho babhūva saḥ ||
meaning: स जातोऽभ्यतपद्देवान् अकस्मादन्धतां गतः | ददुर्देवास्तु तन्नेत्रे ततोऽनन्धो बभूव सः ||
text: He when born distressed the gods, having become suddenly blind. The gods, however, gave him (the use of) his eyes (tannetre); so he was cured of his blindness.

sanskrit_iast: sa vediṣada ityastoc caturbhirjātavedasam | samiddha āpriyo'ntyaindro tamityagneḥ parāṇi ṣaṭ ||
meaning: स वेदिषद इत्यस्तोच् चतुर्भिर्जातवेदसम् | समिद्ध आप्रियोऽन्त्यैन्द्रो तमित्यग्नेः पराणि षट् ||
text: With four (hymns beginning) 'To him seated on the altar' (vedisade: i. 140) he praised Jatavedas (Agni). 'Kindled' (samiddhah: i. 142) is an Apri hymn, its last (stanza) being addressed to Indra (i. 142. 13). The six (i. 145-150) following (beginning) 'Him' (tam: i. 145. 1) are to Agni.

sanskrit_iast: stutau tu mitrāvaruṇau sūktairmitramiti tribhiḥ | mitraṃ maitrīṃ vadanyetām ā dhenavaśca śaṃsati ||
meaning: स्तुतौ तु मित्रावरुणौ सूक्तैर्मित्रमिति त्रिभिः | मित्रं मैत्रीं वदन्येताम् आ धेनवश्च शंसति ||
text: But Mitra-Varuna are praised with the three (151-153) hymns (beginning) 'A Friend' (mitram: i. 151). 'A Friend (mitram: i. 151. 1) expresses that this (stanza) is addressed to Mitra (only). May the kine' (a dhenavah: i. 152. 6)

sanskrit_iast: aditiṃ vāthavāpyagniṃ tathā rūpaṃ hi dṛśyate | agniṃ mene'ditiṃ tveva kutse ceha ca śaunakaḥ ||
meaning: अदितिं वाथवाप्यग्निं तथा रूपं हि दृश्यते | अग्निं मेनेऽदितिं त्वेव कुत्से चेह च शौनकः ||

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣiratra prasaṅgādvā darśanādvānukīrtayet | biṣṇornu kamiti trīṇi vaiṣṇavāni parāṇyataḥ ||
meaning: ऋषिरत्र प्रसङ्गाद्वा दर्शनाद्वानुकीर्तयेत् | बिष्णोर्नु कमिति त्रीणि वैष्णवानि पराण्यतः ||
text: The seer may here mention (Aditi) either incidentally (prasangat) or because he saw (Agni in this form). The three (hymns) after this (i. 154-156), (beginning) Of Visnu now' (visnor nu kam i. 154. 1), are addressed to Visnu; The reading of 19 ab in the text is that of

sanskrit_iast: pra vaśca tisṛbhirṛgbhir indrāviṣṇu saha stutau | gṛhāṇi vā vaiṣṇavāni tā vāmityṛci kāṅkṣati ||
meaning: प्र वश्च तिसृभिरृग्भिर् इन्द्राविष्णु सह स्तुतौ | गृहाणि वा वैष्णवानि ता वामित्यृचि काङ्क्षति ||

sanskrit_iast: jīrṇaṃ tu dīrghatamasaṃ khinnāstatparicāriṇaḥ | dāsā baddhvā nadītoye dṛṣṭihīnamavādadhuḥ ||
meaning: जीर्णं तु दीर्घतमसं खिन्नास्तत्परिचारिणः | दासा बद्ध्वा नदीतोये दृष्टिहीनमवादधुः ||

sanskrit_iast: tatraikastraitano nāma śastreṇainamapāhanat | śiraścāṃsāvuraścaiva svayameva nyakṛntata ||
meaning: तत्रैकस्त्रैतनो नाम शस्त्रेणैनमपाहनत् | शिरश्चांसावुरश्चैव स्वयमेव न्यकृन्तत ||
text: One among them, Traitana by name, tried to strike him away with his sword, and (in so doing) cut to pieces (nyakrntata) his own head, shoulders and breast. i.

sanskrit_iast: hatvā dīrghatamāstaṃ tu pāpena mahatā vṛtama | ātmāṅgānyanudaccaiva tatrodonmohnito bhṛśam ||
meaning: हत्वा दीर्घतमास्तं तु पापेन महता वृतम | आत्माङ्गान्यनुदच्चैव तत्रोदोन्मोह्नितो भृशम् ||
text: Now Dirghatamas having (thus) slain him (who had) involved (himself) in great sin, moved his limbs there (in the river), (though) excessively stupefied (unmohita) by the water (uda).

sanskrit_iast: aṅgadeśasamīpe tu taṃ nadyaḥ samudakṣipan | aṅgarājagṛhe yuktām uśijaṃ putrakāmyayā ||
meaning: अङ्गदेशसमीपे तु तं नद्यः समुदक्षिपन् | अङ्गराजगृहे युक्ताम् उशिजं पुत्रकाम्यया ||
text: Now the currents (nadyah) a threw him up in the neighbourhood of the Anga country. B Usij was employed b in the house of the king of Anga.

sanskrit_iast: rājñā ca prahitāṃ dāsīṃ bhaktāṃ matvā mahātapāḥ | janayāmāsa cotthāya kakṣīvatpramukhānṛṣīn ||
meaning: राज्ञा च प्रहितां दासीं भक्तां मत्वा महातपाः | जनयामास चोत्थाय कक्षीवत्प्रमुखानृषीन् ||

sanskrit_iast: tuṣṭāva caiva sūktābhyām abodhītyaśvināvṛṣiḥ | preti dyāvāpṛthivyau tu parābhyāmetaduttaram ||
meaning: तुष्टाव चैव सूक्ताभ्याम् अबोधीत्यश्विनावृषिः | प्रेति द्यावापृथिव्यौ तु पराभ्यामेतदुत्तरम् ||

sanskrit_iast: kimārbhavaṃ pare mā no medhyasyāśvasya saṃstavaḥ | īrmāntāsa iti tvasyāṃ nīyamānaṃ praśaṃsati ||
meaning: किमार्भवं परे मा नो मेध्यस्याश्वस्य संस्तवः | ईर्मान्तास इति त्वस्यां नीयमानं प्रशंसति ||
text: (beginning) 'Why' (kim: i. 161. 1) is addressed to the Rbhus. The two (162, 163) following (beginning) 'Not us (ma nah i. 162. 1) are a laudation of the sacrificial horse. In the (stanza) Full-haunched' (irmantasah: i. 163. 10) he extols the horse as he is being led.

sanskrit_iast: svayūthyāstasya caivātra bahavaḥ saṃstutā hayāḥ | niyuktāścāniyuktāśca prasaṅgādanukīrtitāḥ ||
meaning: स्वयूथ्यास्तस्य चैवात्र बहवः संस्तुता हयाः | नियुक्ताश्चानियुक्ताश्च प्रसङ्गादनुकीर्तिताः ||
text: And here also (i. 163. 10) the many steeds belonging to his troop (svayuthyah) are praised: both the yoked and unyoked are incidentally (prasangat) mentioned.

sanskrit_iast: saṃjñaptavadasaṃjñaptaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ cāha bhūtavat | tasya māṃsasya sūnasya carūṇāṃ haviṣastathā ||
meaning: संज्ञप्तवदसंज्ञप्तं भविष्यं चाह भूतवत् | तस्य मांसस्य सूनस्य चरूणां हविषस्तथा ||
text: He speaks of him (though) not (yet) sacrificed as (already) sacrificed, of (his) future (state) as if past. Of his flesh (mamsa), of the basket (suna), of the pots (caru), and of the oblation (havis)

sanskrit_iast: vāso'dhivāsasoścātra yadviśasyaṃ ca kīrtitam | gātrasya śūlasthūṇānāṃ svadhiteśca prakīrtanam ||
meaning: वासोऽधिवाससोश्चात्र यद्विशस्यं च कीर्तितम् | गात्रस्य शूलस्थूणानां स्वधितेश्च प्रकीर्तनम् ||

sanskrit_iast: chāgasya kīrtanaṃ cātra indrāpūṣṇoḥ saha stutiḥ | sūktaṃ yadasyavāmīyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ taducyate ||
meaning: छागस्य कीर्तनं चात्र इन्द्रापूष्णोः सह स्तुतिः | सूक्तं यदस्यवामीयं वैश्वदेवं तदुच्यते ||
text: There is here also mention of the goat (chaga) (and) praise at the same time of Indra-Pusan. " The hymn which (begins) Of this benignant' (asya vamasya: i. 164) c is stated to be addressed to the All-gods. chagasya hm'rbfkrº, bhagasya r.

sanskrit_iast: pravādā vidhidhāstatra devānāṃ cātra kīrtanam | sūkte'syarci parokṣoktā vakṣyāmi bhrātarastrayaḥ ||
meaning: प्रवादा विधिधास्तत्र देवानां चात्र कीर्तनम् | सूक्तेऽस्यर्चि परोक्षोक्ता वक्ष्यामि भ्रातरस्त्रयः ||
text: In it are various sayings (pravadah) and here (too) mention of the gods. B In the stanza 'Of this' (asya: i. 164. 1) in the hymn, three brothers a are spoken of in the third person (paroksa)-I will explain (them). 134 tatra, tvatra r, vatra h.

sanskrit_iast: agnistu vāmaḥ palito vāyurbhrātā tu madhyamaḥ | ghṛtapṛṣṭhastṛtīyo'tra sapta vai raśmaya stutāḥ ||
meaning: अग्निस्तु वामः पलितो वायुर्भ्राता तु मध्यमः | घृतपृष्ठस्तृतीयोऽत्र सप्त वै रश्मय स्तुताः ||
text: Now the benignant, grey-haired one is Agni, while the middle brother is Vayu. The third here is butter-backed (ghrtaprstha) (his) seven rays are praised.

sanskrit_iast: parāstu kathayantyagniṃ yathā varṣati pāti ca | ahorātrāndinānmāsān ṛtūṃśca parivartinaḥ ||
meaning: परास्तु कथयन्त्यग्निं यथा वर्षति पाति च | अहोरात्रान्दिनान्मासान् ऋतूंश्च परिवर्तिनः ||
text: But the following (stanzas) tell of Agni, how he rains and protects; and of days and nights (ahoratra), of days (dina), of months, and of revolving seasons.

sanskrit_iast: pañcadhā ca tridhā caiva ṣoḍhā dvādaśadhaiva ca | saṃvatsaraṃ cakravacca parābhiḥ kīrtayatyṛṣiḥ ||
meaning: पञ्चधा च त्रिधा चैव षोढा द्वादशधैव च | संवत्सरं चक्रवच्च पराभिः कीर्तयत्यृषिः ||
text: With the following (stanzas) a the seer celebrates the year (samvatsara) like a wheel (as) fivefold, and threefold, sixfold and twelvefold;

sanskrit_iast: kṣetrajñānaṃ ca dhenuṃ ca gaurīṃ vācaṃ sarasvatīm | dharmaṃ pūrvayugīyaṃ ca sādhyāndevagaṇāṃstathā ||
meaning: क्षेत्रज्ञानं च धेनुं च गौरीं वाचं सरस्वतीम् | धर्मं पूर्वयुगीयं च साध्यान्देवगणांस्तथा ||

sanskrit_iast: vividhāni ca karmāṇi agnivāyuvivasvatām | vibhūtimagnervāyośca jagati sthāsnujaṅgame ||
meaning: विविधानि च कर्माणि अग्निवायुविवस्वताम् | विभूतिमग्नेर्वायोश्च जगति स्थास्नुजङ्गमे ||

sanskrit_iast: haraṇaṃ raśmibhirvāro visargaṃ punareva ca | karmānukīrtanaṃ cātra parjanyāgnivivasvatām ||
meaning: हरणं रश्मिभिर्वारो विसर्गं पुनरेव च | कर्मानुकीर्तनं चात्र पर्जन्याग्निविवस्वताम् ||

sanskrit_iast: mātāputrau tu vākprāṇau mātā vāgitaraḥ sutaḥ | sarasvantamiti prāṇo vācaṃ prāhuḥ sarasvatīm ||
meaning: मातापुत्रौ तु वाक्प्राणौ माता वागितरः सुतः | सरस्वन्तमिति प्राणो वाचं प्राहुः सरस्वतीम् ||
text: Now mother and son are Vac (Speech) and Prana (Breath): the mother is Vac, the son is the other (Prana). by) 'Sarasvata, while Vac they call Sarasvati. k.-39 d= ii. 51.

sanskrit_iast: śarīramindriyairyuktaṃ kṣetramityabhidhīyate | veda tatprāṇa evaikas tasmātkṣetrajña ucyate ||
meaning: शरीरमिन्द्रियैर्युक्तं क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते | वेद तत्प्राण एवैकस् तस्मात्क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते ||
text: The body joined with the organs of sense is designated ksetra. Prana alone knows it: hence he (Prana) is spoken of as 'he who knows the body' (ksetra-jna).

sanskrit_iast: medhe śakastasya dhūmaḥ salilaṃ vāsa eva vā | soma ukṣā bhavantyasya pāvakāśca trayo'dhipāḥ ||
meaning: मेधे शकस्तस्य धूमः सलिलं वास एव वा | सोम उक्षा भवन्त्यस्य पावकाश्च त्रयोऽधिपाः ||
text: Saka is (used) in (the sense of) cloud; its dhuma is water b or garment. The bull d is Soma; and the three lords e (adhipa) are his purifiers f.

sanskrit_iast: gaurīrantaṃ vaiśvadevam upari syātpṛthakstutiḥ | indraṃ mitramime sauryau saurī vāntyā sarasvate ||
meaning: गौरीरन्तं वैश्वदेवम् उपरि स्यात्पृथक्स्तुतिः | इन्द्रं मित्रमिमे सौर्यौ सौरी वान्त्या सरस्वते ||
text: That (part of i. 164) which ends with (the stanza) 'The buffalo' (gaurih: i. 164. 41) is addressed to the All-gods; afterwards there may be (said to be) separate praise (prthak-stuti). sanskrit_iast: sa tānabhijagāmāśu nirupyaindraṃ havistadā | marutaścābhituṣṭāva sūktaistannviti ca tribhiḥ ||

text: He quickly went to them after having prepared (nirupya) an oblation to Indra, and he praised the Maruts a also with the three hymns (i. 166-168) 'Now that' (tan nu: i. 166. 1).

sanskrit_iast: kasyacittvarthasaṃcāre cittameva vinaśyati | kiṃ na ityabravīdindram agastyo bhrātarastava ||

sanskrit_iast: ṛtau snātāmṛṣirbhāryāṃ lopamudrāṃ yaśasvinīm | upajalpitumārebhe rahaḥsaṃyogakāmyayā ||

meaning: निरुक्तं तदिदं वार्यम् इन्द्र श्रेष्ठान्यृचान्त्यया | वव्रे वरमिदं सर्वं तदाकर्ण्य शचीपतिः ||
text: This choice (made by Grtsamada) is explained in the final (6) stanza (of Rg-veda ii. 21), 'O Indra, the best' (indra sresthani): he chose all this as a boon. The Lord of Saci hearing that,

sanskrit_iast: tathetyuktvā turāṣāṭ tu pāṇau jagrāha dakṣiṇe | ṛṣiścāsya sakhitvena pāṇinā pāṇimaspṛśat ||

text: But in the hemistich 'O Sarasvati, thou' (Sarasvati tvam: ii. 30. 8) the Middle Vac (is praised). 'Who us' (yo nah: ii. 30. 9) is (in) praise of Brhaspati; the stanza 'That of yours' (tam vah: ii. 30. 11) is (in) praise of the Maruts.

sanskrit_iast: asmākaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ syād ādāvasyeti cāsya ṛk | dyāvāpṛthivyostvāṣṭryau vā athavaindryau pare tataḥ ||

text: 'Our' (asmakam: ii. 31) should be (regarded as) addressed to the All-gods; and the stanza at the beginning of (the hymn) Of this' (asya: ii. 32. 1) belongs to Heaven and Earth; the two following it (ii. 32. 2, 3) are addressed either to Tvastr or to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: dve dvai rākāsinovālyoḥ ṣaḍ guṅgvādyāstathāntyayā | tatpūrvaṃ dve ṛcau kuhvāḥ kuhūmahamiti smṛte ||

sanskrit_iast: taduttare dve'numataira anu no'nviditi smṛte | dhātuścatasrastatrādo dhātā dadātu no rayim ||

text: Followed by these (taduttare) there are two, anu nah (and) anv it, traditionally held to belong to Anumati. At the beginning in the same place there are four ( stanzas) to Dhatr (beginning) - May the Creator grant us wealth' (dhata dadatu no rajim ).

sanskrit_iast: raudraṃ mārutaṃ tu praram ā te dhārāvarā iti | vāmatastu mṛgaṃ dṛṣṭvā bibhyadetya ṛṣiḥ svayam ||

sanskrit_iast: tubhyamityārtave sūktaṃ sāvitrādāśvinaṃ param | somaḥ pūṣāditiścaiva somapauṣṇe'ntyayā stutāḥ ||

text: There are two hymns (ii. 36, 37) addressed to the Seasons (beginning) To thee' (tubhyam: ii. 36. 1). After one addressed to Savitr (38) follows one to the Asvins (39). With the last (stanza: 6) of (the hymn) to Soma-Pusan (40), Soma, Pusan, and Aditi as well, are praised.

sanskrit_iast: vāyavye caindravāyavī pañcātha prāugāstṛcāḥ | pretyṛkstauti havirdhāne agnistatra nipātabhāk | dyāvāpṛthivyau dyāveti havirdhāne tataḥ pare ||

The stanza Forth' (pra: 19) praises the two Soma carts: Agni is there incidental (nipata-bhaj). Heaven and Earth' (dyava: 20) (praises) Heaven and Earth; then follow (21) the two Soma carts. sanskrit_iast: pra yantu mārutañcāntyā śatadhāraṃ gurustavaḥ | pra vo vājā ṛtūnstauti ṛtvija stauti manthata ||

text: And (the triplet) Let them go forth' (pra yantu: iii. 26. 4-6) is addressed to the Maruts. The last (stanza), 'With a hundred streams' (Satadharam: iii. 26. 9), is (in) praise of a preceptor. 'Forth your food' (pra vo vajah: iii. 27. 1) praises the seasons; 'Rub ye' (manthata: iii. 29. 5) praises the priests.

meaning: सूर्यक्षयादिहाहृत्य ददुस्ते जमदग्नयः | कुशिकानां ततः सा वाग् अमतिं तामपाहनत् ||

sanskrit_iast: upeti cāsyāṃ ca kuśikān viśvāmitro'nubodhayat | labdhvā vācaṃ ca hṛṣṭātmā tānṛṣīnpratyapūjayat ||
meaning: उपेति चास्यां च कुशिकान् विश्वामित्रोऽनुबोधयत् | लब्ध्वा वाचं च हृष्टात्मा तानृषीन्प्रत्यपूजयत् ||
text: And in the ( stanza) 'Hither ' (upa : iii. 53. II) Visvamitra restored the Kusikas to consciousness (anubodhayat). gladdened at heart by receiving Speech he paid homage to those seers (the Jamadagnis), r, - _ upeti casyam mr'

sanskrit_iast: sasarparīriti dvābhyām ṛgbhyāṃ vācaṃ stuvansvayam | sthirāvityanaso'ṅgānyanaḍuhaśca gṛhānvrajan ||
meaning: ससर्परीरिति द्वाभ्याम् ऋग्भ्यां वाचं स्तुवन्स्वयम् | स्थिरावित्यनसोऽङ्गान्यनडुहश्च गृहान्व्रजन् ||

sanskrit_iast: tataśca svaśarīreṇa gṛhāngacchanparīdade | parāścatasro yāstvatra vasiṣṭhadveṣiṇyaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
meaning: ततश्च स्वशरीरेण गृहान्गच्छन्परीददे | पराश्चतस्रो यास्त्वत्र वसिष्ठद्वेषिण्यः स्मृताः ||
text: And then going home he deposited (thema there) in person (svasarirena). 158 But the four stanzas which follow (iii. 53. 21-24 ) are traditionally held to be hostile to the Vasisthas.

sanskrit_iast: viśvāmitreṇa tāḥ proktā abhiśāpā iti smṛtāḥ | dviṣaddveṣāstu tā proktā vidyāścaivābhicārikāḥ ||
meaning: विश्वामित्रेण ताः प्रोक्ता अभिशापा इति स्मृताः | द्विषद्द्वेषास्तु ता प्रोक्ता विद्याश्चैवाभिचारिकाः ||
text: They were pronounced by Visvamitra; they are traditionally held to be imprecations' (abhisapa). They are pronounced to be hostile to enemies a and magical (abhicarika) incantations.

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭhāstā na śṛṇvanti tadācāryakasaṃmatam | kīrtanācchravaṇādvāpi mahādoṣaśca jāyate ||
meaning: वसिष्ठास्ता न शृण्वन्ति तदाचार्यकसंमतम् | कीर्तनाच्छ्रवणाद्वापि महादोषश्च जायते ||
text: The Vasisthas will not listen to them. This is the unanimous opinion of their authorities (acaryaka)a: great guilt arises from repeating or listening (to them); iii.

sanskrit_iast: śatadhā bhidyate mūrdhā kīrtitena śrutena vā | teṣāṃ bālāḥ pramīyante tasmāttāstu na kīrtayet ||
meaning: शतधा भिद्यते मूर्धा कीर्तितेन श्रुतेन वा | तेषां बालाः प्रमीयन्ते तस्मात्तास्तु न कीर्तयेत् ||
text: By repeating or hearing (them) one's head is broken into a hundred fragments; the children of those (who do so) perish: therefore one should not repeat them.

sanskrit_iast: viśvāṃśca devāṃstuṣṭāva caturbhirimamityṛṣiḥ | astaudviśvātmanā sarvān manyamānaḥ paraṃ padam ||
meaning: विश्वांश्च देवांस्तुष्टाव चतुर्भिरिममित्यृषिः | अस्तौद्विश्वात्मना सर्वान् मन्यमानः परं पदम् ||
text: The seer praised the All-gods with the four (hymns) To him' (imam: iii. 54-57). B He praised them all with his whole soul, thinking of the highest Abode, 121 ed is found in B and

sanskrit_iast: devānāmasuratvaṃ tad ekaṃ mahaditīrayan | aśvinau mitra ṛbhavo dhenurmitra iheha vaḥ ||
meaning: देवानामसुरत्वं तद् एकं महदितीरयन् | अश्विनौ मित्र ऋभवो धेनुर्मित्र इहेह वः ||

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvadevīti vijñeyā maitrī mitrāya pañca tu | aindrārbhavastṛcastvatra ārbhave sūkta uttamaḥ ||
meaning: वैश्वदेवीति विज्ञेया मैत्री मित्राय पञ्च तु | ऐन्द्रार्भवस्तृचस्त्वत्र आर्भवे सूक्त उत्तमः ||
text: (The stanza) addressed to Mitra, 'To Mitra five' (mitraya panca: iii. 59. 8), should be recognized as addressed to the All-gods. But the last triplet here in the hymn to the Rbhus (iii. 60.5-7) is addressed to Indra and the Rbhus. 160 tvatrarbhave in all MSS. and r.

sanskrit_iast: pūrve dvṛce nipātīndra uṣo vājena pañcamāt | auṣasāduttarāstvantye ṣaṭ pṛthagdevatāstṛcāḥ | aindrāvaruṇaḥ prathamo bārhaspatyastathāparaḥ ||
meaning: पूर्वे द्वृचे निपातीन्द्र उषो वाजेन पञ्चमात् | औषसादुत्तरास्त्वन्त्ये षट् पृथग्देवतास्तृचाः | ऐन्द्रावरुणः प्रथमो बार्हस्पत्यस्तथापरः ||
text: In the preceding couplet (iii. 60. 3, 4) Indra is incidental. After 'O Usas, with strength' (uso vajena: iii. 61) the fifth (hymn), which is addressed to Dawn, there follow in the final (hymn iii. 62) six triplets addressed to separate deities: the first (1-3) is addressed to Indra -Varuna, and the following one (4-6) to Brhaspati ; - 124 ab is found in

sanskrit_iast: pauṣṇasāvitrasaumyāśca maitrāvaruṇa uttamaḥ | tuṣṭāva jamadagniśca tena devāvṛtāvṛdhau ||
meaning: पौष्णसावित्रसौम्याश्च मैत्रावरुण उत्तमः | तुष्टाव जमदग्निश्च तेन देवावृतावृधौ ||

sanskrit_iast: devarṣipitṛpūjārthaṃ pāpācāntracāṇi yacchunaḥ | yasya vai śyenarūpeṇa āharadvṛtrahā madhu ||
meaning: देवर्षिपितृपूजार्थं पापाचान्त्रचाणि यच्छुनः | यस्य वै श्येनरूपेण आहरद्वृत्रहा मधु ||
text: He (Vamadeva) for whom, when he cooked the entrails of a dog for the sake of honouring the Gods, the Seers, and the Fathers, the Vrtra-slayer (Indra), in the form of an eagle, brought the mead, papacantrani yacchunah Am', ya antranyapacacchunah Bn.

sanskrit_iast: so'gniṃ tu pañcadaśabhir indraṃ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ paraiḥ | ṛṣistvāmiti tuṣṭāva sūktaireti tu gautamaḥ ||
meaning: सोऽग्निं तु पञ्चदशभिर् इन्द्रं षोडशभिः परैः | ऋषिस्त्वामिति तुष्टाव सूक्तैरेति तु गौतमः ||

sanskrit_iast: sa bhrātaramiti tvāsu tisṛṣvagnirnipātabhāk | varuṇenābhisaṃstauti āhuranye nipātinam ||
meaning: स भ्रातरमिति त्वासु तिसृष्वग्निर्निपातभाक् | वरुणेनाभिसंस्तौति आहुरन्ये निपातिनम् ||
text: In the three (stanzas) 'As such, thy brother' (sa bhrataram: iv. 1. 2-4) Agni is incidental (nipatabhaj); others say that (the seer) praises the incidental (nipatin) Agni together with Varuna.

sanskrit_iast: liṅgoktadaivate sūkte eke pratyagnireva tu | ṛṣirbodhaditi dvābhyāṃ stauti somakameva tu ||
meaning: लिङ्गोक्तदैवते सूक्ते एके प्रत्यग्निरेव तु | ऋषिर्बोधदिति द्वाभ्यां स्तौति सोमकमेव तु ||
text: Some (say) that the two hymns 'Agni, upon' (praty agnih: iv. 13, 14) are addressed to the divinities mentioned by their characteristic names (lingoktadaivata). But with the two (stanzas) 'He noted' (bodhat: iv. 15. 7, 8) the seer praises Somaka only. II.

sanskrit_iast: tasyaiva cāyuṣo'rthāya parābhyāmaśvinau stutau | añjasā na janiṣye'haṃ bruvāṇaṃ garbhameva tu ||
meaning: तस्यैव चायुषोऽर्थाय पराभ्यामश्विनौ स्तुतौ | अञ्जसा न जनिष्येऽहं ब्रुवाणं गर्भमेव तु ||
text: And with a view to (long ) life for him the Asvins are praised with the two following ( stanzas : iv. 15. 9, 10). Her unborn child (garbham) who said, "I will not be born in the straightforward way (anjasa)',

sanskrit_iast: anvaśādaditiḥ putram indramātmahitaiṣiṇī | sa jātamātro yuddhāya ṛṣimevājuhāva tu ||
meaning: अन्वशाददितिः पुत्रम् इन्द्रमात्महितैषिणी | स जातमात्रो युद्धाय ऋषिमेवाजुहाव तु ||
text: (that is), her son Indra, Aditi, anxious for her own welfare, admonished ( anvasat). But he (Indra), as soon as born, challenged the seer to fight.

sanskrit_iast: godhayanvāmadevastaṃ kṛtvātmani balaṃ tathā | dināni daśa rātrīśca vijigye cainamojasā ||
meaning: गोधयन्वामदेवस्तं कृत्वात्मनि बलं तथा | दिनानि दश रात्रीश्च विजिग्ये चैनमोजसा ||
text: Vamadeva, engaging him, after he (Indra) had thus done violence to himself (the seer), for ten days and nights, vanquished him with might.

sanskrit_iast: sa taṃ ka imamityasyāṃ vikrīṇannṛṣisaṃsadi | svayaṃ tenāmituṣṭāva nakirindreti gautamaḥ ||
meaning: स तं क इममित्यस्यां विक्रीणन्नृषिसंसदि | स्वयं तेनामितुष्टाव नकिरिन्द्रेति गौतमः ||
text: Gautama, selling a him in the assembly of seers in the (stanza) 'Who this' (ca imam: iv. 24. 10), himself for that iv. 30 purpose (tena)b praised (him with the stanza), 'None, O Indra' (nakir indra: iv. 30.

sanskrit_iast: kimādutāsīti cāsyāṃ manyumardhe parāṇudat | athāsya rūpavīryāṇi dhairyakāryāṇi tānyṛṣiḥ ||
meaning: किमादुतासीति चास्यां मन्युमर्धे पराणुदत् | अथास्य रूपवीर्याणि धैर्यकार्याणि तान्यृषिः ||

sanskrit_iast: vividhāni ca karmāṇi śaśaṃsāditaye tathā | ahamityātmasaṃstāvas tṛce stutirivāsya hi ||
meaning: विविधानि च कर्माणि शशंसादितये तथा | अहमित्यात्मसंस्तावस् तृचे स्तुतिरिवास्य हि ||

sanskrit_iast: pra su ṣa vibhyo navabhir ṛgbhiḥ śyenasya saṃstavaḥ | parābhistveti pañcarce somenendra stutaḥ saha ||
meaning: प्र सु ष विभ्यो नवभिर् ऋग्भिः श्येनस्य संस्तवः | पराभिस्त्वेति पञ्चर्चे सोमेनेन्द्र स्तुतः सह ||
text: With the following nine stanzas (beginning) 'Before all birds this' (pra su sa vibhyah: iv. 26. 4-7; 27. 1-5) there is praise of the eagle. In the hymn of five stanzas 'Thee' (tva: iv. 28) Indra is praised together with Soma.

sanskrit_iast: somapradhānāmaitāṃ tu krauṣṭukirmanyate stutim | divaściditi caitena tṛcenendreṇa saṃstutām ||
meaning: सोमप्रधानामैतां तु क्रौष्टुकिर्मन्यते स्तुतिम् | दिवश्चिदिति चैतेन तृचेनेन्द्रेण संस्तुताम् ||
text: Kraustuki regards this praise to be chiefly addressed to Soma; while with the triplet 'Even of the Sky' (divas cid: iv. 30. 6-11) the teacher Sakatayana considered the middle Dawn 164 to be praised with Indra. And in the stanza here 'Good wealth' (vamam : iv. 30. 24 ) Bhaga, Pusan, and Aryaman are

sanskrit_iast: uṣasaṃ madhyamāṃ mene ācāryaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ | vāmamṛci stutāścātra bhagaḥ pūṣeti cāryamā ||
meaning: उषसं मध्यमां मेने आचार्यः शाकटायनः | वाममृचि स्तुताश्चात्र भगः पूषेति चार्यमा ||

sanskrit_iast: karūḻatīti pūṣokto'dantakaḥ sa iti śruteḥ | asmākamuttamaṃ sūryaṃ stautityāhāśvalāyanaḥ ||
meaning: करूḻअतीति पूषोक्तोऽदन्तकः स इति श्रुतेः | अस्माकमुत्तमं सूर्यं स्तौतित्याहाश्वलायनः ||
text: Pusan is (here) called 'Karulatin ' : according to Vedic text (sruti) b he is 'toothless.' asvalayana says that (the stanza) 'Of us most excellent' (asmakam uttamam : iv. 31. 15) praises the Sun.

sanskrit_iast: indrasya harayo hyaśvā agneraśvāstu rohitaḥ | sūryasya haritaścaiva vāyorniyuta eva ca ||
meaning: इन्द्रस्य हरयो ह्यश्वा अग्नेरश्वास्तु रोहितः | सूर्यस्य हरितश्चैव वायोर्नियुत एव च ||
text: The horses of Indra are Bays (hari), the horses of Agni are Ruddy ones ( rohit) ; those of Surya are Fallows (harit ), and those of Vayu Teams (niyut).

sanskrit_iast: rāsabhaḥ sahito'śvibhyām ajāḥ pūṣṇaśca vājinaḥ | pṛṣatyo'śvāstu marutāṃ gāvo'ruṇyastathoṣasām ||
meaning: रासभः सहितोऽश्विभ्याम् अजाः पूष्णश्च वाजिनः | पृषत्योऽश्वास्तु मरुतां गावोऽरुण्यस्तथोषसाम् ||
text: The Ass a is associated (sahita) with the Asvins, and Goats are the steeds (vajin) of Pusan, but Dappled mares (prsati) are the horses of the Maruts, while ruddy (aruni) Cows are those of the Dawns.

sanskrit_iast: saviturvājinaḥ śyāvā viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ | sahaite devatābhistu stūyante'pyalpaśo'nyathā ||
meaning: सवितुर्वाजिनः श्यावा विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः | सहैते देवताभिस्तु स्तूयन्तेऽप्यल्पशोऽन्यथा ||
text: The steeds of Savity are Duns (syavah); the Multiform (visvarupa) a is (the steed) of Brhaspati. Now these too are praised with (their) deities, otherwise b but seldom.

sanskrit_iast: āyuṣaṃ vāhanaṃ cāpi stutau yasyeha dṛśyate | tameva tu stutaṃ vidyāt tasyātmā bahudhā hi saḥ ||
meaning: आयुषं वाहनं चापि स्तुतौ यस्येह दृश्यते | तमेव तु स्तुतं विद्यात् तस्यात्मा बहुधा हि सः ||
text: (The god) whose weapon and vehicle appear here in a laudation should be recognized as the one praised; for that (god) is in many ways the soul (atman) of it.

sanskrit_iast: kanīnakā tūktaśeṣo haryo stutirihocyate | cātvāryataśca vijñeyānyū apragṛhyāṇi vidradhe ||
meaning: कनीनका तूक्तशेषो हर्यो स्तुतिरिहोच्यते | चात्वार्यतश्च विज्ञेयान्यू अप्रगृह्याणि विद्रधे ||
text: 'Two small girls' (kaninaka: iv. 32. 23, 24), the remainder of the hymn, is here called a praise of the two Bays (of Indra). And the four (words) after it, (viz.) vidradhe (and the rest) are to be recognized as liable to phonetic combination (apragrhyani)d.

sanskrit_iast: preti pañcārbhavaṃ trīṇi dādhikrāṇi parāṇyataḥ | ṛgdyāvāpṛthivyau stauti dādhikrāṇāṃ mukhe tu yā ||
meaning: प्रेति पञ्चार्भवं त्रीणि दाधिक्राणि पराण्यतः | ऋग्द्यावापृथिव्यौ स्तौति दाधिक्राणां मुखे तु या ||
text: (With) Forth' (pra: iv. 33. 1) begins a group of five hymns addressed to the Rbhus (iv. 33-37). Following that are three (hymns) addressed to Dadhikra (iv. 38-40); but the stanza which is at the head of the hymns addressed to Dadhikra (iv. 38. 1) praises Heaven and Earth.

sanskrit_iast: parokṣairamuto vāgbhira nāmabhiśca stutāstrayaḥ | agnirvāyuśca sūryaśca haṃsaḥ śuciṣadityṛci ||
meaning: परोक्षैरमुतो वाग्भिर नामभिश्च स्तुतास्त्रयः | अग्निर्वायुश्च सूर्यश्च हंसः शुचिषदित्यृचि ||
text: Then with indirect (paroksa) expressions (vac) and names the three, Agni, Vayu, Surya, are praised in the stanza, 'The Swan dwelling in light' (hamsah sucisat: iv. 50. 5).

sanskrit_iast: niyuktā sūryadevatyā haṃsa ityaitareyake | dvai tvaindrāvaruṇe sūkte tatastrīṇyāśvināni kaḥ ||
meaning: नियुक्ता सूर्यदेवत्या हंस इत्यैतरेयके | द्वै त्वैन्द्रावरुणे सूक्ते ततस्त्रीण्याश्विनानि कः ||
text: In the Aitareya (Brahmana) 'The Swan' (hamsah: iv. 40. 5) is prescribed as having Surya for its deity. Now (there follow) two hymns addressed to Indra -Varuna (iv. 41, 42), then three (iv. 43-45) addressed to the Asvins (beginning) 'Who?' (kah: iv. 43. 1).

sanskrit_iast: agraṃ vāyo vihītyeṣu vāyavyāḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ | nava caivendravāyavyā indrastisraḥ śatena ṣaṭ ||
meaning: अग्रं वायो विहीत्येषु वायव्याः सप्त कीर्तिताः | नव चैवेन्द्रवायव्या इन्द्रस्तिस्रः शतेन षट् ||
text: In the (hymns) 'The best' (agram: iv. 46. 1), 'O Vayu' (vayo: iv. 47. 1), 'Enjoy' (vihi: iv. 48. 1-5) seven stanzas are declared to be addressed to Vayu; and nine are addressed to Indra - Vayu, (viz.) 'Indra' (indrah: iv. 47. 2-4) being three, (and) 'With a hundred' (satena: iv. 46. 2-7) being six. iv.

sanskrit_iast: idaṃ kathitadevatyaṃ yastastambhottamo dvṛcaḥ | stutirindrābṛhaspatyor aṣṭāvetā ṛcaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
meaning: इदं कथितदेवत्यं यस्तस्तम्भोत्तमो द्वृचः | स्तुतिरिन्द्राबृहस्पत्योर् अष्टावेता ऋचः स्मृताः ||
text: 'This' (idam: iv. 49), addressed to the deities mentioned in it, (and) the last couplet (10, 11) of 'He who has propped (yas tastambha: iv. 50)-these eight stanzas b are traditionally held to be (in) praise of Indra-Brhaspati.

sanskrit_iast: sūktaṃ tu tadbārhaspatyam idamityauṣase pare | purodhātuḥ karmaśaṃsā sa indrājocyate tṛce ||
meaning: सूक्तं तु तद्बार्हस्पत्यम् इदमित्यौषसे परे | पुरोधातुः कर्मशंसा स इन्द्राजोच्यते तृचे ||
text: That a hymn, however, is addressed to Brhaspati ; the two next (beginning) 'That' (idam: iv. 51, 52) are addressed to Usas. In the triplet 'Surely that king' (sa id raja: iv. 50. 7-9) laudation of the function of the appointer of priests (purodhatuh) is expressed.

text: (In the case) of the application of a formula and the formula (itself), the application is the more important. There should be careful observation of the rule (vidhi) regarding the two. The formulas should be (regarded as) making (only) statements (abhidhayaka)a.

sanskrit_iast: dyāvāpṛthivyau savitā indrāsomau bṛhaspatiḥ | pṛthakpṛthak paraiḥ sūktaiḥ somārudreti tau stutau ||

text: Discus, car, jewel, wife, territory, horse, and elephantthese are the seven treasures of all emperors (cakravartin).

sanskrit_iast: abhigamyocatustau taṃ prasādyākhyāya nāmanī | yudhi vāraśivairbrahmann āvāṃ viddhi vinirjitau ||

sanskrit_iast: bhavatpurohitāvāvāṃ kṣatrabandhūñjayevahi | kṣatraṃ tadapi vijñeyaṃ brahma yatpāti śāśvatam ||

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣistau tu tathetyuktvā pāyuṃ putramabhāṣata | adharṣaṇīyau śatrūṇāṃ kuruṣvaitau nṛpāviti ||

sanskrit_iast: prathamā tvasya sūktasya yoddhāraṃ stauti varmiṇam | dhanuṣaśca dvitīyā tu tṛtīyā jyābhimantriṇī ||

text: The first (stanza) of this hymn praises the warrior in his coat of mail (1), the second is (in praise) of the bow (2), the third consecrates the bowstring (3).

sanskrit_iast: stautyṛgārtnī tu iṣudhiṃ stauti pañcamī | ardhena sārathiḥ ṣaṣṭhyā raśmayo'rdhena saṃstutaḥ ||

text: (These were) Bhaga, Aryaman, and Amsa, Mitra and Varuna, Dhatr and Vidhatr, and Vivasvat of great brilliance,

sanskrit_iast: tvaṣṭā pūṣā tathaivendro dvādaśo viṣṇurucyate | dvandvaṃ tasyāstu tajjajñe mitraśca varuṇaśca ha ||
meaning: त्वष्टा पूषा तथैवेन्द्रो द्वादशो विष्णुरुच्यते | द्वन्द्वं तस्यास्तु तज्जज्ञे मित्रश्च वरुणश्च ह ||

sanskrit_iast: tayorādityayoḥ sattre dṛṣṭvāpsarasamurvaśīm | retaścaskanda tatkumbhe nyapatadvāsatīvare ||
