meaning: तेनैव तु मुहूर्तेन वीर्यवन्तौ तपस्विनौ | अगस्त्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षी संबभूवतः ||
text: Now at that same moment two vigorous ascetics, the seers Agastya a and Vasistha, there came into being. a On the story of the birth of Agastya see Sieg, Sagenstoffe, pp. 105-108.

sanskrit_iast: bahudhā patite śukre kalaśe'tha jale sthale || sthale vasiṣṭhastu muniḥ saṃbhūta ṛṣisattamaḥ ||
meaning: बहुधा पतिते शुक्रे कलशेऽथ जले स्थले || स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः संभूत ऋषिसत्तमः ||
text: Now the semen having fallen in various ways-in a jar, in water, on the ground-the sage Vasistha, best of seers, was produced on the ground; patite sukre mrfkn, patitam retah bs.

sanskrit_iast: kumbhe tvagastyaḥ saṃbhūto jale matsyo mahādyutiḥ | udiyāya tato'gastyaḥ śamyāmātro mahāyaśāḥ ||
meaning: कुम्भे त्वगस्त्यः संभूतो जले मत्स्यो महाद्युतिः | उदियाय ततोऽगस्त्यः शम्यामात्रो महायशाः ||

sanskrit_iast: mānena saṃmito yasmāt tasmānmānya ihocyate | yadvā kumbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kumbhenāpi hi mīyate ||
meaning: मानेन संमितो यस्मात् तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते | यद्वा कुम्भादृषिर्जातः कुम्भेनापि हि मीयते ||
text: Because he was meted with a measure, he is here called Manya; or else (because) the seer was born from a jar. For measurement is made with a jar also: hi

sanskrit_iast: kumbha ityabhidhānaṃ tu parimāṇasya lakṣyate | tato'psu guhyamāṇāsu vasiṣṭhaḥ puṣkare sthitaḥ ||
meaning: कुम्भ इत्यभिधानं तु परिमाणस्य लक्ष्यते | ततोऽप्सु गुह्यमाणासु वसिष्ठः पुष्करे स्थितः ||

sanskrit_iast: nāmāsya guṇato jajñe vasateḥ śraiṣṭhyakarmaṇaḥ | adṛśyamṛṣibhirhīndraṃ so'paśyattapasā purā ||
meaning: नामास्य गुणतो जज्ञे वसतेः श्रैष्ठ्यकर्मणः | अदृश्यमृषिभिर्हीन्द्रं सोऽपश्यत्तपसा पुरा ||
text: His name arose, with reference to his virtue (gunatah), from the root vas expressive of pre-eminence: for he once upon a time, by means of austerity, saw Indra who was invisible to (other) seers.

sanskrit_iast: somabhāgānatho tasmai provāca harivāhanaḥ | ṛṣayo vā indramiti brāhmaṇāttaddhi dṛśyate ||
meaning: सोमभागानथो तस्मै प्रोवाच हरिवाहनः | ऋषयो वा इन्द्रमिति ब्राह्मणात्तद्धि दृश्यते ||
text: The Lord of Bay Steeds (Indra) then proclaimed to him (that he should receive) shares in Soma. B For this appears from the Brahmana (passage) 'The seers (saw not) Indra' (rsayo va indram). somabhaganatha Am', somabhagamstatas B.

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭhaśca vasiṣṭhāśca brāhmaṇā brahmakarmaṇi | sarvakarmasu yajñeṣu dakṣiṇīyatamāstathā ||
meaning: वसिष्ठश्च वसिष्ठाश्च ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मकर्मणि | सर्वकर्मसु यज्ञेषु दक्षिणीयतमास्तथा ||
text: Vasistha and the Vasisthas thus (became) Brahmans in the office of Brahman priest, most worthy of fees in all rites at sacrifices. vasisthasca vasisthasca B, vasisthasca vasisthasca Am'.

sanskrit_iast: tasmādye'dyāpi vāsiṣṭhāḥ sadasyāḥ syustu karhicit | arhayeddakṣiṇābhistān bhāllaveyī śrutistviyam ||
meaning: तस्माद्येऽद्यापि वासिष्ठाः सदस्याः स्युस्तु कर्हिचित् | अर्हयेद्दक्षिणाभिस्तान् भाल्लवेयी श्रुतिस्त्वियम् ||
text: Therefore one should honour with fees all such descendants of Vasistha who may at any time even to-day be present at a sacrificial assembly, so (says) a sacred text of the Bhallavins. ye'dyapi Am 1, adyapi B.

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣistu maitrāvaruṇiḥ sūktaiḥ ṣoḻaśabhiḥ paraiḥ | tuṣṭāvāgnimiti tvagnim āpryastatra juṣasva naḥ ||
meaning: ऋषिस्तु मैत्रावरुणिः सूक्तैः षोḻअशभिः परैः | तुष्टावाग्निमिति त्वग्निम् आप्र्यस्तत्र जुषस्व नः ||
text: Now the seer, the son of Mitra-Varuna (Vasistha), with the following sixteen a hymns (beginning) 'Agni' (agnim: vii. 1. 1) praised Agni; Enjoy our' (jusasva nah: vii. 2) here are Apri stanzas.

sanskrit_iast: prāgnaye'tha pra samrājo dvitīyaṃ prāgnaye tṛcam | vaiśvānarīyāṇyetāni tve haindrāṇi parāṇyataḥ ||
meaning: प्राग्नयेऽथ प्र सम्राजो द्वितीयं प्राग्नये तृचम् | वैश्वानरीयाण्येतानि त्वे हैन्द्राणि पराण्यतः ||
text: Then 'Forth to Agni' (pragnaye: vii. 5), 'Forth of the sovereign lord' (pra samrajah: vii. 6), the second Forth to Agni' (pragnaye: vii. 13) which consists of three stanzas-these are addressed to Vaisvanara. Then those which follow, (beginning) 'In thee, indeed' (tve ha: vii. 18), are addressed to Indra, 162. being fifteen hymns (vii. 18-32): praise of the Maruts is incidental (in them). In the (stanza) 'No one Sudass' (nakih sudasah vii. 32. 10) the gift of Paijavana (Sudas)

sanskrit_iast: daśa pañca ca sūktāni nipāto marutāṃ stutiḥ | nakiḥ sudāsa ityasyāṃ dānaṃ paijavanasya tu ||
meaning: दश पञ्च च सूक्तानि निपातो मरुतां स्तुतिः | नकिः सुदास इत्यस्यां दानं पैजवनस्य तु ||

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭhena caturbhistu dve napturiti kīrtitam || saṃvādaṃ sūktamaindraṃ vā śvityañcastu pracakṣate ||
meaning: वसिष्ठेन चतुर्भिस्तु द्वे नप्तुरिति कीर्तितम् || संवादं सूक्तमैन्द्रं वा श्वित्यञ्चस्तु प्रचक्षते ||

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭhāgastyayoratra kīrtyate tanayaiḥ saha | indreṇa caiva saṃvādo mahimā janma karma ca ||
meaning: वसिष्ठागस्त्ययोरत्र कीर्त्यते तनयैः सह | इन्द्रेण चैव संवादो महिमा जन्म कर्म च ||
text: Here is proclaimed a dialogue of Vasistha and Agastya with their sons and also with Indra, and (their) greatness, birth, and action (are celebrated).

sanskrit_iast: parāṇi preti catvāri vaiśvadevāni tatra tu | stotyṛgabjāmahiṃ tatra mā no'hiṃ budhnyameva ca ||
meaning: पराणि प्रेति चत्वारि वैश्वदेवानि तत्र तु | स्तोत्यृगब्जामहिं तत्र मा नोऽहिं बुध्न्यमेव च ||
text: The following four (hymns) 'Forth' (pra: vii. 34-37) are addressed to the All-gods. There, however, the stanza 'Born in the waters' (abjam: vii. 34. 16) praises the Dragon (ahi), and there 'May us not' (ma nah: vii. 34. 17) (praises) the Dragon of the Deep (ahi budhnya).

sanskrit_iast: ahirāhanti meghānsa eti vā teṣu madhyamaḥ | yo'hiḥ sa budhnyo vudhne hi ṇo'ntarikṣe'bhijāyate ||
meaning: अहिराहन्ति मेघान्स एति वा तेषु मध्यमः | योऽहिः स बुध्न्यो वुध्ने हि णोऽन्तरिक्षेऽभिजायते ||
text: The Dragon (ahi) strikes (ahanti) the clouds, or he goes in the midst among them. The Dragon is of the deep (budhnya), for he is born in the deep (budhna), the air.

sanskrit_iast: udu ṣya savituḥ sūktaṃ śaṃ no vājinadaivataḥ | dvṛco'rdharcaśca bhāgo'tra bhagamugra iti śrutiḥ ||
meaning: उदु ष्य सवितुः सूक्तं शं नो वाजिनदैवतः | द्वृचोऽर्धर्चश्च भागोऽत्र भगमुग्र इति श्रुतिः ||
text: On high that' (ud u syah: vii. 38) is a hymn of Savitr. Here the couplet Blessed for us' (sam nah: vii. 38. 7, 8) has Steeds as its divinities, and the hemistich 'On Bhaga the mighty' (bhagam ugrah: vii. 38. 6 cd) is addressed to Bhaga, so a sacred text (states). I.

sanskrit_iast: pādaścaiva tṛtīyo'tra pañcamyāmahidaivataḥ | yathārdharco bhagamugras tathā nūnaṃ bhago'pi ca ||
meaning: पादश्चैव तृतीयोऽत्र पञ्चम्यामहिदैवतः | यथार्धर्चो भगमुग्रस् तथा नूनं भगोऽपि च ||
text: And the third verse in the fifth (stanza) here (vii. 38. 5°) a has the Dragon for its divinity. B As the hemistich 'On Bhaga the mighty' (bhagam ugrah: vii. 38.6 cd), so also is Now Bhaga' (nunam bhagah: vii. 38.

sanskrit_iast: sa hi ratnāni savitā suvātīti bhagaḥ sa vā | vaiśvadevāni pañcordhvaḥ pañcarco bhagadaivataḥ ||
meaning: स हि रत्नानि सविता सुवातीति भगः स वा | वैश्वदेवानि पञ्चोर्ध्वः पञ्चर्चो भगदैवतः ||

sanskrit_iast: prātarjitamuṣasyāntyā draṣṭṛbhyo'trāśireva vā | eke tu drātarityasyāṃ bhagameva pracakṣate ||
meaning: प्रातर्जितमुषस्यान्त्या द्रष्टृभ्योऽत्राशिरेव वा | एके तु द्रातरित्यस्यां भगमेव प्रचक्षते ||
text: (beginning) 'Winning at morn' (pratarjitam : vii. 41.2-6). The last (stanza) is addressed to Dawn (vii. 41. 7), or else a prayer a for the seers (drastr) b is here (expressed ). Some, however, pronounce Bhaga only to be (the deity) in the ( stanza) - At morn' (pratal : vii. 41.1 ) .

sanskrit_iast: ādāvante tu ṛṣayaḥ kīrtayanti prasaṅgataḥ | sūkte'smindevatāstvanyā anyāstatra bhavanti ca ||
meaning: आदावन्ते तु ऋषयः कीर्तयन्ति प्रसङ्गतः | सूक्तेऽस्मिन्देवतास्त्वन्या अन्यास्तत्र भवन्ति च ||
text: Now the seers at the beginning and end (of hymns) proclaim (deities) in an occasional manner & (prasangatah) : (thus) in this hymn there are some deities (here) and others (there) in that place (tatra)b.

sanskrit_iast: sālokyātsāhacaryādvā saṃstavādathavā punaḥ | gaṇasthānādbhaktito vā kīrtyante'nyāstu devatāḥ ||
meaning: सालोक्यात्साहचर्याद्वा संस्तवादथवा पुनः | गणस्थानाद्भक्तितो वा कीर्त्यन्तेऽन्यास्तु देवताः ||
text: Other deities are proclaimed because they belong to the same world or because they are associated, or else again because they share praise (samstavat), because of the sphere of (their accompanying) troop (gana)b, or because of (common) attribute (bhaktital)..

sanskrit_iast: dādhikramatha sāvitraṃ raudramityanupūrvaśaḥ | dādhike prathamāyāstu devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||
meaning: दाधिक्रमथ सावित्रं रौद्रमित्यनुपूर्वशः | दाधिके प्रथमायास्तु देवताः परिकीर्तिताः ||
text: Next (come) one (hymn) addressed to Dadhikra (vii. 44), one to Savitr (vii. 45), one to Rudra (vii. 46) in succession. But the deities proclaimed as belonging to the first (stanza) of (the hymn) addressed to Dadhikra (vii. 44. 1)

sanskrit_iast: tā jñeyā āpa āpyaṃ syād ārbhavaḥ prathamastṛcaḥ | uttamā vaiśvadevī vā ārbhavī vā nigadyate ||
meaning: ता ज्ञेया आप आप्यं स्याद् आर्भवः प्रथमस्तृचः | उत्तमा वैश्वदेवी वा आर्भवी वा निगद्यते ||

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvadeve tathā śāstre ārbhavaṃ śasyate hi tat | daśame'hni samastaṃ samudrajyeṣṭhā apāṃ stutiḥ ||
meaning: वैश्वदेवे तथा शास्त्रे आर्भवं शस्यते हि तत् | दशमेऽह्नि समस्तं समुद्रज्येष्ठा अपां स्तुतिः ||
text: For it is thus that this entire (hymn) addressed to the Rbhus is chanted on the tenth day in the litany to the All-gods. "Whose chief the sea' (samudrajyesthah vii. 49) is (in) praise of the Waters.

sanskrit_iast: ā māmiti tu sūktena pratyṛcaṃ devatā stutāḥ | mitravaruṇāvagniśca devā nadyastathaiva ca ||
meaning: आ मामिति तु सूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं देवता स्तुताः | मित्रवरुणावग्निश्च देवा नद्यस्तथैव च ||
text: Now with the hymn Guard me' (a mam: vii. 50) the deities are praised in successive stanzas: B Mitra-Varuna (1), and Agni (2), the (All)-gods (3), as well as the Rivers (4). m'r,

sanskrit_iast: tṛcāvādityadevatyau rodasyoḥ preti yastṛcaḥ | vāstoṣpatyaścatasrastu sapta prasvāpinyaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
meaning: तृचावादित्यदेवत्यौ रोदस्योः प्रेति यस्तृचः | वास्तोष्पत्यश्चतस्रस्तु सप्त प्रस्वापिन्यः स्मृताः ||
text: Two triplets (vii. 51, 52) have the Adityas for their deities. The triplet which (begins) Forth' (pra: vii. 53. 1-3) is to the Two Worlds (rodasi). There are (then) four (stanzas: vii. 54. 1-3, 55. 1) addressed to Vastospati; the seven (following: vii. 55. 2-8) are traditionally held to be lullaby stanzas.

sanskrit_iast: paraṃ catvāri sūktāni mārutāni ka īmiti | teṣāṃ tu pitaraṃ devaṃ tryambakaṃ stautyṛguttamā ||
meaning: परं चत्वारि सूक्तानि मारुतानि क ईमिति | तेषां तु पितरं देवं त्र्यम्बकं स्तौत्यृगुत्तमा ||
text: After this there are four hymns addressed to the Maruts (beginning) 'Who, pray?' (ka im: vii. 56-59); the last stanza of these (vii. 59. 12) praises Tryambaka, the divine father. param Am', tatah B.

sanskrit_iast: stutau tu mitrāvaruṇau sūktairyaditi saptabhiḥ | aśvinau tu parairdevāv aṣṭabhiḥ prati vāmiti ||
meaning: स्तुतौ तु मित्रावरुणौ सूक्तैर्यदिति सप्तभिः | अश्विनौ तु परैर्देवाव् अष्टभिः प्रति वामिति ||
text: With the seven hymns beginning 'When' (yat: vii. 60-66) Mitra-Varuna are praised; but with the following eight (beginning) 'To meet your' (prati vam: vii. 67-74) the divine Asvins.

sanskrit_iast: yadadyaikotsūryastisra udvetītyardhapañcamāḥ | sauryastaccakṣuriti tu gīyate cakṣurdevatā ||
meaning: यदद्यैकोत्सूर्यस्तिस्र उद्वेतीत्यर्धपञ्चमाः | सौर्यस्तच्चक्षुरिति तु गीयते चक्षुर्देवता ||
text: (In) 'When to-day' (yad adya: vii. 60) one (1), (in) 'Aloft the sun' (ut suryah: vii. 62) three (1-3), (in) 'Aloft he goes' (ud veti: vii. 63) four and a half (1-5 ab) are addressed to Surya, while (in) 'That eye' (tac caksuh: vii. 66. 16) a the eye (of the sun) is sung as the deity.

sanskrit_iast: ādityānāṃ tadvo adya dve ṛcau śaunako'bravīt | anyāḥ sarvā ṛcaḥ sauryo yadadyādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
meaning: आदित्यानां तद्वो अद्य द्वे ऋचौ शौनकोऽब्रवीत् | अन्याः सर्वा ऋचः सौर्यो यदद्याद्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ||
text: Saunaka has stated that the two stanzas 'Thus of you to-day' (tad vo adya: vii. 66. 12, 13) belong to the Adityas, while all the other stanzas, ' When to-day' (yad adya: vii. 66. 4-11) and the rest, are proclaimed (by him) a to be addressed to Surya. .

sanskrit_iast: ime cetāra ityādyāḥ satre mitro mitaḥ stutaḥ | aryamṇo varuṇasyāpi mitrasyaitā nava smṛtāḥ ||
meaning: इमे चेतार इत्याद्याः सत्रे मित्रो मितः स्तुतः | अर्यम्णो वरुणस्यापि मित्रस्यैता नव स्मृताः ||
text: These chastisers' (ime cetarah vii. 60. 5) and the rest... these nine are traditionally held to belong to Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna.

sanskrit_iast: yadadya sūra ityādyā daśādityā ṛcaḥ smṛtāḥ | savitā vāditirmitro varuṇaścāryamā bhagaḥ ||
meaning: यदद्य सूर इत्याद्या दशादित्या ऋचः स्मृताः | सविता वादितिर्मित्रो वरुणश्चार्यमा भगः ||
text: The ten stanzas beginning When to-day the sun's' (yad adya surah: vii. 66. 4-13) are traditionally held to be addressed to the Adityas; or else Savitr, Aditi, Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman, Bhaga

sanskrit_iast: stutā udu tyadityetās tisraḥ sauryastataḥ parāḥ | āśīstaccakṣurityetām ācāryaḥ śaunako'bravīt ||
meaning: स्तुता उदु त्यदित्येतास् तिस्रः सौर्यस्ततः पराः | आशीस्तच्चक्षुरित्येताम् आचार्यः शौनकोऽब्रवीत् ||

sanskrit_iast: uṣāstu saptabhirvyuṣāḥ sūktānyebhyaḥ parāṇi tu | catvārīndrāvaruṇeti indrāvaruṇayo stutiḥ ||
meaning: उषास्तु सप्तभिर्व्युषाः सूक्तान्येभ्यः पराणि तु | चत्वारीन्द्रावरुणेति इन्द्रावरुणयो स्तुतिः ||
text: Now Dawn (is praised) with the seven (hymns) 'Forth the Dawn' (vy usah: vii. 75-81); but the four hymns following these, 'O Indra and Varuna' (indravaruna: vii. 82-85), are (in) praise of Indra-Varuna.

sanskrit_iast: udu jyotiriti tvasminn ardharce madhyama stutaḥ | varuṇasya gṛhānnātrau vasiṣṭhaḥ svapna ācarat ||
meaning: उदु ज्योतिरिति त्वस्मिन्न् अर्धर्चे मध्यम स्तुतः | वरुणस्य गृहान्नात्रौ वसिष्ठः स्वप्न आचरत् ||
text: In the hemistich Aloft the light' (ud u jyotih vii. 76. 1 ab) the Middle (Agni) is praised. During a the night Vasistha in a dream b approached the house of Varuna. - 11 ab is not found in A or

sanskrit_iast: prāviveśātha taṃ tatra śvā nadannabhyadhāvata | krandantaṃ sārameyaṃ sa dhāvantaṃ daṣṭusudyatam ||
meaning: प्राविवेशाथ तं तत्र श्वा नदन्नभ्यधावत | क्रन्दन्तं सारमेयं स धावन्तं दष्टुसुद्यतम् ||
text: He then entered. A dog there ran at him, barking. B Pacifying the hound which was making a din and running (up) with intent to bite, he lulled him to sleep (vyasusvapat) with the two (stanzas) When, O bright one' (yad arjuna: vii. 55. 2, 3). ( He sent him b as well as the other attendants of Varuna to sleep.

sanskrit_iast: yadarjuneti ca dvābhyāṃ sāntvayitvā vyasuṣvapat | sa taṃ prasvāpayāmāsa janamanyaṃ ca vāruṇam ||
meaning: यदर्जुनेति च द्वाभ्यां सान्त्वयित्वा व्यसुष्वपत् | स तं प्रस्वापयामास जनमन्यं च वारुणम् ||

sanskrit_iast: tatastu varuṇo rājā svaiḥ pāśaiḥ pratyabadhyata | sa baddhaḥ pitaraṃ sūktaiś caturbhirita uttaraiḥ ||
meaning: ततस्तु वरुणो राजा स्वैः पाशैः प्रत्यबध्यत | स बद्धः पितरं सूक्तैश् चतुर्भिरित उत्तरैः ||
text: Then king Varuna bound a him with his fetters. Bound (thus) he (Vasistha) praised his father (Varuna) with the next (itah) b following four (hymns) 'The wise' (dhira: vii. 86-89). Then his father released him. A As soon as the (stanza) Thee in the fixed' (dhruvasu tva: vii. 88. 7) had been uttered, the fetters dropped (pramocire)c from him. svaih pasaih pratyabadhyata Am' (prati om ' ), svanpasanpratyamuncata Bn.

sanskrit_iast: abhituṣṭāva dhīreti mumocairna tataḥ pitā | dhruvāsu tveti coktāyāṃ pāśā asmātpramocire ||
meaning: अभितुष्टाव धीरेति मुमोचैर्न ततः पिता | ध्रुवासु त्वेति चोक्तायां पाशा अस्मात्प्रमोचिरे ||

sanskrit_iast: parāṇi trīṇi saktāni vāyavyāni pra vīrayā | atra tāstvaindravāyavyā stutau yāsu dvivatstutiḥ ||
meaning: पराणि त्रीणि सक्तानि वायव्यानि प्र वीरया | अत्र तास्त्वैन्द्रवायव्या स्तुतौ यासु द्विवत्स्तुतिः ||
text: The next three hymns, Forth with longing for the heroes' (pra viraya: vii. 90-92), are addressed to Vayu. Now in this praise those (stanzas) are addressed to Indra-Vayu in which there is praise in the dual (dvivat). tastvai॰ Am', tascai ° B.

sanskrit_iast: pra vīrayoktā vāyavyā prāugītyaitareyake | padasya vyatyayaṃ kṛtvā vāyoḥ prādhānyamucyate ||
meaning: प्र वीरयोक्ता वायव्या प्राउगीत्यैतरेयके | पदस्य व्यत्ययं कृत्वा वायोः प्राधान्यमुच्यते ||
text: Forth with longing for the heroes' (pra viraya: vii. is spoken of in the Aitareya (Brahmana) a as a stanza addressed to Vayu belonging to the Prauga litany (praagi): the predominance of Vayu is (thereby) expressed in contravention (vyatyayam krtva) of one of its verses (pada).

sanskrit_iast: te satyena tṛco yāvat taraścaturṛcaḥ punaḥ | uśantaikā pra sotā carga dvayoretā nava smṛtāḥ ||
meaning: ते सत्येन तृचो यावत् तरश्चतुरृचः पुनः | उशन्तैका प्र सोता चर्ग द्वयोरेता नव स्मृताः ||
text: 'These with true' (te satyena: vii. 90. 5-7) being a triplet, 'As long as strength' (yavat tarah: vii. 91. 4-7), again, being a quatrain, 'Eager' (usanta: vii. 91. 2), being one, and the stanza Forth the presser' (pra sota: vii. 92. 2)-these are traditionally held to be the nine (stanzas) belonging to the two (Indra-Vayu).

sanskrit_iast: endrāgne śucimityete preti sārasvate pare | ṛcā sarasvān sa iti janīyantaśca tisṛbhiḥ ||
meaning: एन्द्राग्ने शुचिमित्येते प्रेति सारस्वते परे | ऋचा सरस्वान् स इति जनीयन्तश्च तिसृभिः ||
text: The two (hymns) 'The pure' (sucim: vii. 93,94) are addressed to Indra-Agni; the two following, 'Forth' (pra: vii. 95, 96), are addressed to Sarasvati. Sarasvat (is praised) with the stanza 'He' (sah: vii. 95. 3) and with the three 'Longing for wives' (janiyantah: vii. 96. 4-6).

sanskrit_iast: rājā varṣasahasrāya dīkṣiṣyannāhuṣaḥ purā | cacāraikarathenemāṃ bruvan sarvāḥ samudragāḥ ||
meaning: राजा वर्षसहस्राय दीक्षिष्यन्नाहुषः पुरा | चचारैकरथेनेमां ब्रुवन् सर्वाः समुद्रगाः ||
text: King Nahusa a in former days wishing to consecrate himself for a thousand years, travelled over this (earth) with a single chariot, saying to all

sanskrit_iast: yakṣye vahata bhāgānme dvandvaśo vāthavaikaśaḥ | pratyūcustaṃ nṛpaṃ nadyaḥ svalpavīryāḥ kathaṃ vayam ||
meaning: यक्ष्ये वहत भागान्मे द्वन्द्वशो वाथवैकशः | प्रत्यूचुस्तं नृपं नद्यः स्वल्पवीर्याः कथं वयम् ||
text: 'I am about to offer sacrifice; bring me shares (for it), either in pairs or singly.' The rivers replied to the king: How can we, who have but very little power,

sanskrit_iast: vahema bhāgātsarvāṃste satre vāryasahasrike | sarasvatīṃ prapadyasva sā te vakṣyati nāhuṣa ||
meaning: वहेम भागात्सर्वांस्ते सत्रे वार्यसहस्रिके | सरस्वतीं प्रपद्यस्व सा ते वक्ष्यति नाहुष ||

sanskrit_iast: tathetyuktvā jagāmāśu āpagāṃ sa sarasvatīm | sā cainaṃ pratijagrāha duduhe ca payo ghṛtam ||
meaning: तथेत्युक्त्वा जगामाशु आपगां स सरस्वतीम् | सा चैनं प्रतिजग्राह दुदुहे च पयो घृतम् ||
text: Saying 'So be it,' he quickly went to the river Sarasvati; and she received him and yielded (duduhe) (him) milk (and) ghee. jagamasu Am', jagamatha B.

sanskrit_iast: etadatyadbhutaṃ karma sarasvatyā nṛpaṃ prati | vāruṇiḥ kīrtayāmāsa prathamasya dvitīyayā ||
meaning: एतदत्यद्भुतं कर्म सरस्वत्या नृपं प्रति | वारुणिः कीर्तयामास प्रथमस्य द्वितीयया ||
text: This exceedingly marvellous act of the Sarasvati towards the king, the son of Varuna (Vasistha) proclaimed with the second (stanza) of the first (of the two hymns, viz. vii. 95. 2). No MS. marks the end of the varga; but that it ends here is indicated by the fact that the figure u is in b placed after 26 ab, which in that MS. by mistake ends similarly, viz. prathamasya trtiyaya (see critical note on 26).

sanskrit_iast: yajñe bārhaspatyamaindraṃ vaiṣṇave tu pare tataḥ | urumaindryaśca tisraḥ syuḥ pārjanye tisra uttare ||
meaning: यज्ञे बार्हस्पत्यमैन्द्रं वैष्णवे तु परे ततः | उरुमैन्द्र्यश्च तिस्रः स्युः पार्जन्ये तिस्र उत्तरे ||
text: 'In the sacrifice' (yajne: vii. 97) is addressed to Brhaspati; (then comes) (hymn) addressed to Indra (vii. 98); but the two following (99, 100) after that are addressed to Visnu, and the vii. 104 three (stanzas) 'Wide' (urum: vii. 99. 4-6) should be (regarded as) addressed to Indra as well. The two next (hymns) Three' (tisrah: 101, 102) are addressed to Parjanya.

sanskrit_iast: stautīndraṃ prathamā tvatra dvitīyādyā bṛhaspatim | yajña ādyendramevāstaud antyā tvindrābṛhaspatī ||
meaning: स्तौतीन्द्रं प्रथमा त्वत्र द्वितीयाद्या बृहस्पतिम् | यज्ञ आद्येन्द्रमेवास्तौद् अन्त्या त्विन्द्राबृहस्पती ||
text: Now the first (stanza) here (vii. 97. 1) praises Indra, the second and the rest (2, 4-8) (praise) Brhaspati. B In 'At the sacrifice' (yajne: vii. 97) the first (stanza) praised Indra alone, but the last both Indra and Brhaspati. is the reading of Am1; instead of this line

sanskrit_iast: tṛtīyā navamī caiva stautīndrābrahmaṇaspati | saṃvatsaraṃ tu maṇḍūkān aindrāsomaṃ paraṃ tu yat ||
meaning: तृतीया नवमी चैव स्तौतीन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पति | संवत्सरं तु मण्डूकान् ऐन्द्रासोमं परं तु यत् ||
text: The third and the ninth (vii. 97. 3, 9) praise Indra and Brahmanaspati. (The hymn) For a year' (samvatsaram: vii. 103) (praises) the frogs; but that which follows (vii. 104) is addressed to Indra-Soma.

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣirdadarśa rākṣoghnaṃ putraśokapariplutaḥ | hate putraśate tasmin saudāsairduḥkhitastadā ||
meaning: ऋषिर्ददर्श राक्षोघ्नं पुत्रशोकपरिप्लुतः | हते पुत्रशते तस्मिन् सौदासैर्दुःखितस्तदा ||
text: The seer, when his hundred sons had been slain by the followers of Sudas, full of pain and overwhelmed with grief for his sons, saw (this hymn) for the destruction of demons II.

sanskrit_iast: ye pākaśaṃsamṛksaumyā āgneyī tat uttarā | ekādaśī vaiśvadevī saumyastasyāḥ paro dvṛcaḥ ||
meaning: ये पाकशंसमृक्सौम्या आग्नेयी तत् उत्तरा | एकादशी वैश्वदेवी सौम्यस्तस्याः परो द्वृचः ||
text: The stanza 'Who the simple' (ye pakasamsam: vii. 104. 9) is addressed to Soma; the next (10) after that is addressed to Agni; the eleventh is addressed to the All-gods (11); the couplet which follows it (12, 13) is addressed to Soma.

sanskrit_iast: yadi vāhamṛgāgneyī aindrī yo meti tu smṛtā | grāvṇī pra yā jigātoti vi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ tu mārutī ||
meaning: यदि वाहमृगाग्नेयी ऐन्द्री यो मेति तु स्मृता | ग्राव्णी प्र या जिगातोति वि तिष्ठध्वं तु मारुती ||
text: The stanza 'As if I' (yadi vaham: vii. 104. 14) is addressed to Agni, while Who me' (yo ma: 16) is traditionally held to be addressed to Indra; 'She who strides forth' (pra ya jigati: 17) is addressed to the pressing stones, while 'Spread out' (vi tisthadhvam: 18) is addressed to the Maruts.

sanskrit_iast: pra vartayeti pañcendrya pendrāsomī tvṛguttamā | ṛṣistvāśiṣamāśāste mā no rakṣa iti tvṛci ||
meaning: प्र वर्तयेति पञ्चेन्द्र्य पेन्द्रासोमी त्वृगुत्तमा | ऋषिस्त्वाशिषमाशास्ते मा नो रक्ष इति त्वृचि ||
text: Five (stanzas, beginning) Hurl forth' (pra vartaya: vii. 104. 19-22, 24) are addressed to Indra, while the last stanza is addressed to Indra-Soma. In the stanza 'May not the demon us' (ma no raksas: 23) the seer invokes a blessing

sanskrit_iast: divi caiva pṛthivyāṃ ca tathā pālanamātmanaḥ | ulūkayātuṃ jahyetān nānārūpānniśācarān ||
meaning: दिवि चैव पृथिव्यां च तथा पालनमात्मनः | उलूकयातुं जह्येतान् नानारूपान्निशाचरान् ||

sanskrit_iast: pañcadaśyāṃ tu sūktasya aṣṭamyāṃ caiva vāruṇiḥ | duḥkhaśokaparītātmā śapate vilapanniva ||
meaning: पञ्चदश्यां तु सूक्तस्य अष्टम्यां चैव वारुणिः | दुःखशोकपरीतात्मा शपते विलपन्निव ||
text: Now in the fifteenth and in the eighth ( stanza) of the hymn the son of Varuna (Vasistha), while as it were lamenting, his soul being overwhelmed with pain and grief, utters a curse. suktasya astamyam hd, (°sya )

sanskrit_iast: hate putraśate tasmin vasiṣṭho duḥkhitastadā | rakṣobhūtena śāpāttu sudāseneti vai śrutiḥ ||
meaning: हते पुत्रशते तस्मिन् वसिष्ठो दुःखितस्तदा | रक्षोभूतेन शापात्तु सुदासेनेति वै श्रुतिः ||
text: Vasistha was at that time pained, as his hundred sons had been slain by Sudasa a who, in consequence of a curse, had been transformed into a demon (raksas); such is the sacred tradition.

sanskrit_iast: aṣṭama maṇḍala kaṇvaścaiva pragāthaśca ghoraputrau babhūvatuḥ | guruṇā tāvanujñātāv ūṣatuḥ sahitau vane ||
meaning: अष्टम मण्डल कण्वश्चैव प्रगाथश्च घोरपुत्रौ बभूवतुः | गुरुणा तावनुज्ञाताव् ऊषतुः सहितौ वने ||

sanskrit_iast: vasatostu tayostatra kaṇvapatnyā śiraḥ svapat | kṛtvā kanīyānkaṇvasya utsaṅge nānvabudhyata ||
meaning: वसतोस्तु तयोस्तत्र कण्वपत्न्या शिरः स्वपत् | कृत्वा कनीयान्कण्वस्य उत्सङ्गे नान्वबुध्यत ||
text: Now while these two dwelt there the younger (brother) of Kanva (i.e. Pragatha), having placed his head while asleep (svapat) a on the lap of Kanva's wife, did not awake.

sanskrit_iast: śaptukāmastu taṃ kaṇvaḥ kruddhaḥ pāpābhiśaṅkayā | bodhayāmāsa pādena didhakṣanniva tejasā ||
meaning: शप्तुकामस्तु तं कण्वः क्रुद्धः पापाभिशङ्कया | बोधयामास पादेन दिधक्षन्निव तेजसा ||
text: Now Kanva, enraged by suspicion of a sin (and) wishing to curse him, awakened him with his foot, as though about to consume him with his fiery energy.

sanskrit_iast: viditvā tasya taṃ bhāvaṃ pragāthaḥ prāñjali sthitaḥ | mātṛtve ca pitṛtve ca varayāmāsa tāvubhau ||
meaning: विदित्वा तस्य तं भावं प्रगाथः प्राञ्जलि स्थितः | मातृत्वे च पितृत्वे च वरयामास तावुभौ ||
text: Pragatha, becoming aware of his intention, stood with folded hands and chose the couple for his mother and father. tam

sanskrit_iast: sa ghauro vātha kāṇvo vā vaṃśajairbahubhiḥ saha | dadarśānyaiśca sahita ṛṣirmaṇḍalamaṣṭamam ||
meaning: स घौरो वाथ काण्वो वा वंशजैर्बहुभिः सह | ददर्शान्यैश्च सहित ऋषिर्मण्डलमष्टमम् ||
text: The seer, being (thus) the son of either Ghora or Kanva, saw, in company with many other members of his family, the eighth Mandala.

sanskrit_iast: mācidaindrāṇi catvāri anvasya sthūramityṛci | tuṣṭāvāṅgirasī nārī vasantī śāśvatī patim ||
meaning: माचिदैन्द्राणि चत्वारि अन्वस्य स्थूरमित्यृचि | तुष्टावाङ्गिरसी नारी वसन्ती शाश्वती पतिम् ||
text: There are four hymns addressed to Indra (beginning) 'Not at all' (ma cit: viii. 1-4) in the stanza 'Downward his mighty' (anv asya sthuram: viii. 1. 34), Sasvati, daughter of Angiras, living (vasanti) a as his wife (nari), praised her husband.

sanskrit_iast: striyaṃ santaṃ pumāṃsaṃ tam āsaṅgaṃ kṛtavānṛṣiḥ | svasya dānaṃ stuhītyṛgbhiś caturbhiḥ parikīrtitam ||
meaning: स्त्रियं सन्तं पुमांसं तम् आसङ्गं कृतवानृषिः | स्वस्य दानं स्तुहीत्यृग्भिश् चतुर्भिः परिकीर्तितम् ||
text: The seer turned that Asanga, who had been a woman, into a man (again). With the four b stanzas Praise' (stuhi: viii. 1. 30-33) his own gift (to the seer) is proclaimed (by Asanga).

sanskrit_iast: śikṣetyṛgbhyāṃ tu kāśyasya vibhindoḥ parikīrtitam | pākasthāmnastu bhojasya caturbhiryamiti stutam ||
meaning: शिक्षेत्यृग्भ्यां तु काश्यस्य विभिन्दोः परिकीर्तितम् | पाकस्थाम्नस्तु भोजस्य चतुर्भिर्यमिति स्तुतम् ||
text: But with the two stanzas Bestow' (siksa: viii. 2. 41, 42) that of Vibhindu, king of Kasi (kasya)a, is proclaimed, while with the four (stanzas) 'Which' (yam: viii. 3. 21-24) the (gift) of the liberal Pakasthaman is praised.

sanskrit_iast: pauṣṇau preti pragāthau dvau manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ | aindramevātha pūrvaṃ tu gālavaḥ pauṣṇamuttaram ||
meaning: पौष्णौ प्रेति प्रगाथौ द्वौ मन्यते शाकटायनः | ऐन्द्रमेवाथ पूर्वं तु गालवः पौष्णमुत्तरम् ||
text: The two pragatha couplets (beginning) Forth' (pra: viii. 4. 15-18) Sakatayana thinks are addressed to Pusan; Galava, however, (thinks) the former (15, 16) is addressed to Indra only, the latter (17, 18) to Pusan.

sanskrit_iast: aindrāṇāmiha sūktānām uttamasyottame tṛce | dānaṃ rājñaḥ kuruṅgasya sthūraṃ rāya iti stutam ||
meaning: ऐन्द्राणामिह सूक्तानाम् उत्तमस्योत्तमे तृचे | दानं राज्ञः कुरुङ्गस्य स्थूरं राय इति स्तुतम् ||
text: In the last triplet of the last of the Indra hymns here (viii. 4. 19-21), the gift of king Kurunga is praised (with the words) 'Abundant wealth' (sthuram radhah: 19).

sanskrit_iast: dūrādityāśvine sūkte saptatriṃśattamī yathā | ityardharco dvṛcaścāntyaḥ kaśordānastutiḥ smṛtā ||
meaning: दूरादित्याश्विने सूक्ते सप्तत्रिंशत्तमी यथा | इत्यर्धर्चो द्वृचश्चान्त्यः कशोर्दानस्तुतिः स्मृता ||
text: In the hymn addressed to the Asvins, 'From afar' (durat: viii. 5), the thirty-seventh stanza, (that is) the hemistich 'As' (yatha: 37), and the final couplet (38, 39) are traditionally held to be (in) praise of the gifts of Kasu.

sanskrit_iast: mahānaindraṃ pratnavatyām agniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ stutam | manyate śākapūṇistu bhārmyaśvaścaiva mudgalaḥ ||
meaning: महानैन्द्रं प्रत्नवत्याम् अग्निं वैश्वानरं स्तुतम् | मन्यते शाकपूणिस्तु भार्म्यश्वश्चैव मुद्गलः ||
text: 'Great' (mahan: viii. 6) is addressed to Indra: in (the stanza) containing (the word) 'ancient' (pratna: viii. 6. 30), Sakapuni, as well as Mudgala, son of Bhrmyasva, thinks Agni Vaisvanara is praised.

sanskrit_iast: tṛce tu śatamityasmin dānaṃ tairindiraṃ smṛtam | paraṃ nu mārutaṃ preti ā nastrīṇyāśvināni ca ||
meaning: तृचे तु शतमित्यस्मिन् दानं तैरिन्दिरं स्मृतम् | परं नु मारुतं प्रेति आ नस्त्रीण्याश्विनानि च ||

sanskrit_iast: nipātamāha devānāṃ dātā ma hati bhāguriḥ || ṛcaṃ yāskastṛcaṃ tvetaṃ manyate vaiśvadevatam | ādityadaivataṃ sūktaṃ tyānnvityatra paraṃ tu yat ||

text: Yaska, however, considers this triplet (viii. 65. 10-12) to be addressed to the All-gods. But the hymn which here follows, 'Now these' (tyan nu: viii. 67), has the Adityas as its divinities.

sanskrit_iast: dhīvarāḥ sahasā mīnān dṛṣṭvā sārasvate jale | jālaṃ prakṣipya tānbaddhvod akṣipansalilātsthalam ||

text: Fishermen, having by chance seen fish in the water of the Sarasvati, cast a net, caught them, and threw them upon a the dry land out of the water.

sanskrit_iast: dhīvarāḥ kṣudbhayaṃ mā vo bhūt svargaṃ prāptyatheti ca | uteti mātā tatraiṣāṃ tṛcenābhiṣṭutāditiḥ ||

sanskrit_iast: mātṛtvādabhisaṃbandhāt stūyetaiṣāṃ stutau stutau | aindrāṇyā tvā rathaṃ trīṇi stautyṛtūnupa meti ṣaṭ ||

text: Because she is their mother she may be praised in every praise of them owing to (this) connexion. 'Hither thee as a car' (a tva ratham: viii. 68-70) are three hymns addressed to Indra; (the stanza) 'Near to me six' (upa ma sat: viii. 68. 14) a praises the seasons.

Thou' (tvam: viii. 71, 72) are two (hymns) addressed to Agni; or the latter hymn (72) is (in) praise of oblations, rksasvamedhayoratra hd (rksasvamedhayor S), asrasvamedhayoratra m'r, arcapatya- svamedhaya, arttapatvyasvamedhaya f.

text: In the couplet 'When Vac' (yad vak: 10, 11) he (the seer) praises the divine all-pervading Vac. Having a tormented these three worlds Vrtra remained (unassailable) by reason of his fury.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ nāśakaddhantumindro viṣṇumabhyetya so'bravīt | vṛtraṃ haniṣye tiṣṭhasva vikramyādya mamāntike ||
meaning: तं नाशकद्धन्तुमिन्द्रो विष्णुमभ्येत्य सोऽब्रवीत् | वृत्रं हनिष्ये तिष्ठस्व विक्रम्याद्य ममान्तिके ||
text: Him Indra could not slay. Going to Visnu he said, 'I wish to slay Vrtra; stride forth to-day and stand at my side.

sanskrit_iast: udyatasyaiva vajrasya dyaurdadātu mamāntaram | tatheti viṣṇustaccakre dyauścāsya vivaraṃ dadau ||
meaning: उद्यतस्यैव वज्रस्य द्यौर्ददातु ममान्तरम् | तथेति विष्णुस्तच्चक्रे द्यौश्चास्य विवरं ददौ ||
text: May Dyaus make room (antara) for my outstretched bolt.' Saying 'Yes,' Visnu did so, and Dyaus gave him an opening (vivara).

sanskrit_iast: tadetadakhilaṃ proktaṃ sakhe viṣṇaviti tvṛci | maitrāvaruṇyaḥ sūktādyāś catasrastvṛdhagityṛcaḥ ||
meaning: तदेतदखिलं प्रोक्तं सखे विष्णविति त्वृचि | मैत्रावरुण्यः सूक्ताद्याश् चतस्रस्त्वृधगित्यृचः ||
text: All this is proclaimed in the stanza 'Friend Visnu' (sakhe visno: viii. 100. 12). But the first four stanzas of the hymn (beginning) Specially' (rdhak: viii. 101. 1-4) are addressed to Mitra-Varuna; proktam B 9, sarva A.

sanskrit_iast: preti mitrāya pādāśca aryamṇo varuṇasya ca | trayaścaturthaḥ sarveṣām ādityānāmiti stutiḥ ||
meaning: प्रेति मित्राय पादाश्च अर्यम्णो वरुणस्य च | त्रयश्चतुर्थः सर्वेषाम् आदित्यानामिति स्तुतिः ||

sanskrit_iast: parā tvādityadevatyā ā ma ityaśvino dvṛcaḥ | vāyavye saurye uṣasyā prabhāṃ vā candrasūryayoḥ ||
meaning: परा त्वादित्यदेवत्या आ म इत्यश्विनो द्वृचः | वायव्ये सौर्ये उषस्या प्रभां वा चन्द्रसूर्ययोः ||
text: But the following stanza (6) has the Adityas as its deities. 'Hither to me' (a me: 7, 8) is a couplet addressed to the Asvins; there are (then) two addressed to Vayu (9, 10), two to Surya (11, 12), one to Usas (13), or (the seer here praises) the light a of the sun and moon.

sanskrit_iast: pāvamānī prajā heti mātetyṛgbhyāṃ tu gau stutā | tvamagne bṛhadāgneye pare'gnistvṛci saṃstutaḥ ||
meaning: पावमानी प्रजा हेति मातेत्यृग्भ्यां तु गौ स्तुता | त्वमग्ने बृहदाग्नेये परेऽग्निस्त्वृचि संस्तुतः ||
text: 'Generations truly' (praja ha: 14) is addressed to Pavamana, while with the two stanzas 'The mother' (mata: 15, 16) the Cow is praised. 'Thou, O Agni, great' (tvam agne brhat: 'Thou, ix. 67 viii. 102, 103) are two hymns addressed to Agni. But in a stanza of the latter (pare) is praised Agni, 128. the Middle, together with the Maruts and Rudras, (viz. in) Come, O Agni' (agne yahi: viii. 103. 14). B Or in the first hemistich, 'Generations truly' (praja ha: viii. 101. 14), Agni is here named, in B only.

sanskrit_iast: marudbhiḥ saha rudraiśca āgne yāhīti madhyamaḥ | prajā hetyapi vārdharce prathame'gnirihocyate ||
meaning: मरुद्भिः सह रुद्रैश्च आग्ने याहीति मध्यमः | प्रजा हेत्यपि वार्धर्चे प्रथमेऽग्निरिहोच्यते ||

sanskrit_iast: pāde tṛtīya ādityas turīye madhyama stutaḥ | ruhasye brāhmaṇe'pyevaṃ vyākhyataṃ hyaitareyake ||
meaning: पादे तृतीय आदित्यस् तुरीये मध्यम स्तुतः | रुहस्ये ब्राह्मणेऽप्येवं व्याख्यतं ह्यैतरेयके ||

sanskrit_iast: navama maṇḍala pavamāna stutaḥ somo navame tviha maṇḍale | pavamānavadāpryastu samiddha iti saṃstutāḥ ||
meaning: नवम मण्डल पवमान स्तुतः सोमो नवमे त्विह मण्डले | पवमानवदाप्र्यस्तु समिद्ध इति संस्तुताः ||
text: Now Soma Pavamana is praised here in the ninth Mandala. (In the hymn) 'Kindled' (samiddhah: ix. 5) the Apri deities (apryah) are praised like Pavamana.

sanskrit_iast: atra āyūṃṣīti cāsu tisṛṣvagnirnipātabhāk | avitā na iti tvasmiṃs tṛce pūṣṇā saha stutaḥ ||
meaning: अत्र आयूंषीति चासु तिसृष्वग्निर्निपातभाक् | अविता न इति त्वस्मिंस् तृचे पूष्णा सह स्तुतः ||
text: And in the three stanzas 'O Agni, life' (agna ayumsi: ix. 66. 19-21), Agni is incidental (nipatabhaj), while in the triplet 'Our protector' (avita nah: ix. 67. 10-12) he (Pavamana) a is praised together with Pusan. * Pusan is directly mentioned in 10, indirectly as kapardin in II, and aghrni in 12; ayam somah pavate occurs in II, ayam pavate in 12; cp. Sarvanukramani: avita nas tisrah pausnyo va, that is, the three stanzas 10-12 are addressed to Pusan or Pavamana. ..

sanskrit_iast: āgneyyau dve ṛcāvatra yatta ityuttare tataḥ | ubhābhyāmiti sāvitrī āgnisāvitryṛguttarā ||
meaning: आग्नेय्यौ द्वे ऋचावत्र यत्त इत्युत्तरे ततः | उभाभ्यामिति सावित्री आग्निसावित्र्यृगुत्तरा ||
text: Then two later stanzas in this hymn (atra), 'which of thee' (yat te: ix. 67. 23, 24), are addressed to Agni; 'By both of these' (ubhabhyam: 25) is addressed to Savitr; the next stanza (26) is addressed to Agni and Savitra. savitri

sanskrit_iast: punantu māṃ vaiśvadevī āgneyī tvṛgupa priyam | uttare ca va ityete svādhyāyādhyetṛ saṃstavaḥ ||
meaning: पुनन्तु मां वैश्वदेवी आग्नेयी त्वृगुप प्रियम् | उत्तरे च व इत्येते स्वाध्यायाध्येतृ संस्तवः ||
text: May they purify me' (punantu ma: ix. 67. 27) is addressed to the All-gods, while the stanza 'Near to the friend' (upa priyam: 29) is addressed to Agni, and the two next, Who' (yah: 31, 32), are (in) praise of the student of recitation (svadhyayadhyetr). a uttare ca ya

sanskrit_iast: sūkte nirukte srakve'gnī rakṣohā dharmasaṃstavaḥ | sūryaḥvaccātmavaccāpi pavitramiti cocyate ||
meaning: सूक्ते निरुक्ते स्रक्वेऽग्नी रक्षोहा धर्मसंस्तवः | सूर्यःवच्चात्मवच्चापि पवित्रमिति चोच्यते ||
text: In the hymn 'At the rim' (srakve: ix. 73), when interpreted (nirukte), the demon-slaying Agnib (is spoken of), and 'The filter' (pavitram: ix. 83) is called a praise of the Kettle (gharma) as (representing) the Sun (surya) and the Soul (atman).

sanskrit_iast: ārbhavastu bhavetpāda ṛbhurdhīra iti smṛtaḥ | nipātaistu tribhiḥ pādais trayo devā ihoditāḥ ||
meaning: आर्भवस्तु भवेत्पाद ऋभुर्धीर इति स्मृतः | निपातैस्तु त्रिभिः पादैस् त्रयो देवा इहोदिताः ||
text: The verse 'Deft, wise' (rbhur dhirah: ix. 87. 3) should be held to be addressed to Rbhu. Now three gods are here b mentioned incidentally (nipata) in three verses (pada)

sanskrit_iast: brahmā devānāṃ tisroktās tribhistvetairdvṛcairdvṛcaiḥ | sūryavaccātmavaccāpi stūyate soma eva vā ||
meaning: ब्रह्मा देवानां तिस्रोक्तास् त्रिभिस्त्वेतैर्द्वृचैर्द्वृचैः | सूर्यवच्चात्मवच्चापि स्तूयते सोम एव वा ||

sanskrit_iast: anāvṛṣṭyāṃ tu vartantyāṃ papraccharṣīñchacīpatiḥ | kāle durge mahatyasmin karmaṇā kena jīvatha ||
meaning: अनावृष्ट्यां तु वर्तन्त्यां पप्रच्छर्षीञ्छचीपतिः | काले दुर्गे महत्यस्मिन् कर्मणा केन जीवथ ||
text: Now while a drought was prevailing, the Lord of Saci asked (the) seersa, 'In this great time of distress, by what activity do you live

sanskrit_iast: śakaṭaṃ śākinī gāvaḥ kṛṣirasyandanaṃ vanam | samudraḥ parvato rājā evaṃ jīvāmahe vayam ||
meaning: शकटं शाकिनी गावः कृषिरस्यन्दनं वनम् | समुद्रः पर्वतो राजा एवं जीवामहे वयम् ||
text: 'A cart, a field, kine, tillage, water that does not flow away (asyandana), a forest, the sea, a mountain, a king-by these means (evam) we live

sanskrit_iast: stuvanneva śaśaṃsāsya ṛṣirāṅgirasaḥ śiśuḥ | nānānīyena sūktena ṛṣīṇāmeva saṃnidhau ||
meaning: स्तुवन्नेव शशंसास्य ऋषिराङ्गिरसः शिशुः | नानानीयेन सूक्तेन ऋषीणामेव संनिधौ ||
text: In praising (Indra) the seer Sisu, son of Angiras, declared (this) to him with the hymn Variously' (nananam: ix. 112) in the presence of the (other) seers.

sanskrit_iast: tānindrastvāha sarvāṃstu tapadhvaṃ sumahattapaḥ | na hyṛte tapasaḥ śakyam idaṃ kṛchraṃ vyapohitum ||
meaning: तानिन्द्रस्त्वाह सर्वांस्तु तपध्वं सुमहत्तपः | न ह्यृते तपसः शक्यम् इदं कृछ्रं व्यपोहितुम् ||
text: Now to all of them Indra said: 'Do ye perform very severe penance; for without penance this distress cannot be removed.'

sanskrit_iast: atha te vai tapastepuḥ sarve svargajigīṣavaḥ | tataste tapasogreṇa pāvamānīrṛco'bruvan ||
meaning: अथ ते वै तपस्तेपुः सर्वे स्वर्गजिगीषवः | ततस्ते तपसोग्रेण पावमानीरृचोऽब्रुवन् ||
text: Now all of them, desirous of obtaining heaven, performed penance. Then in consequence of fierce austerity they pronounced stanzas relating to (Soma) Pavamana (pavamani).

sanskrit_iast: anasūyuradhīyānaḥ śuśrūṣustapasānvitaḥ | daśa pūrvāparān vaṃśyān punātyātmānameva ca ||
meaning: अनसूयुरधीयानः शुश्रूषुस्तपसान्वितः | दश पूर्वापरान् वंश्यान् पुनात्यात्मानमेव च ||
text: One who is not envious, is studious, obedient, and practises penance, purifies ten ascendants and descendants as well as himself.

sanskrit_iast: pāpaṃ yaccākarotkiṃcan manovāgdehabhojanaiḥ | pūtaḥ sa tasmātsarvasmāt svādhyāyaphalamaśnute ||
meaning: पापं यच्चाकरोत्किंचन् मनोवाग्देहभोजनैः | पूतः स तस्मात्सर्वस्मात् स्वाध्यायफलमश्नुते ||
text: And whatever sin he has committed with mind, speech, body, and food-purified from all that, he enjoys the fruit of Vedic study a yacca

sanskrit_iast: pāvamānyaḥ paraṃ brahma śukraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam | gāyatryo'nte'tra yaścāsāṃ prāṇānāyamya tanmanāḥ ||
meaning: पावमान्यः परं ब्रह्म शुक्रं ज्योतिः सनातनम् | गायत्र्योऽन्तेऽत्र यश्चासां प्राणानायम्य तन्मनाः ||
text: The Pavamani Gayatrisa are the supreme Brahma, the bright, eternal light. He who here at his latter end (ante), restraining his breathe, intent on them, a m'r, hd.-This sloka is not found in B, but in A and

sanskrit_iast: pāvamānaṃ pitṝndevān dhyāyedyaśca sarasvatīm | pitṝṃstasyopavarteta kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakam ||
meaning: पावमानं पितॄन्देवान् ध्यायेद्यश्च सरस्वतीम् | पितॄंस्तस्योपवर्तेत क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकम् ||

sanskrit_iast: etatsūktaśataṃ saumyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ sacaturdaśam | pāvamānamiti khyātam anuvākāstu sapta vai ||
meaning: एतत्सूक्तशतं सौम्यं मण्डलं सचतुर्दशम् | पावमानमिति ख्यातम् अनुवाकास्तु सप्त वै ||
text: This Mandala, addressed to Soma, containing one hundred and fourteen hymns, is called 'Pavamana,' and seven lessons (anuvaka) are (contained in it)a.

sanskrit_iast: daśama maṇḍala saptāgneyāni sūktāni dadarśātha ḍati tritaḥ | pra ketuneti tvāṣṭrastu triśirāḥ sūktamuttaram ||
meaning: दशम मण्डल सप्ताग्नेयानि सूक्तानि ददर्शाथ डति त्रितः | प्र केतुनेति त्वाष्ट्रस्तु त्रिशिराः सूक्तमुत्तरम् ||
text: Trita saw seven hymns addressed to Agni (beginning), 'Before' (agre: x. 1-7), but Trisiras, son of Tvastr, the next hymn (beginning) 'Forth with his banner' (pra ketuna: x. 8).

sanskrit_iast: ṛcastvasya ṣaḻāgneyyas tṛcastvasyeti yaḥ paraḥ | tenendramabhituṣṭāva svaprānta iti naḥ śrutiḥ ||
meaning: ऋचस्त्वस्य षḻआग्नेय्यस् तृचस्त्वस्येति यः परः | तेनेन्द्रमभितुष्टाव स्वप्रान्त इति नः श्रुतिः ||
text: Now six (stanzas) of this (hymn) are addressed to Agni (x. 8. 1-6), while with the triplet which follows, 'Of him' (asya: 7-9), he praised Indra at the end of a dream: such is our sacred tradition.

sanskrit_iast: abhavatsa hi devānāṃ purodhāḥ priyakāmyayā | asurāṇāṃ svasuḥ putras triśirā viśvarūpadhṛk ||
meaning: अभवत्स हि देवानां पुरोधाः प्रियकाम्यया | असुराणां स्वसुः पुत्रस् त्रिशिरा विश्वरूपधृक् ||
text: Trisiras, who could assume all forms (visvarupadhrk), being the son of a sister of the Asuras, became the domestic priest of the gods from a desire of (rendering) a service (to the former). sa hi

sanskrit_iast: tamṛṣiṃ prahitaṃ tvindro deveṣu bubudhe'suraiḥ | so'sya vajreṇa tānyāśu śirāṃsi trīṇyathāchidat ||
meaning: तमृषिं प्रहितं त्विन्द्रो देवेषु बुबुधेऽसुरैः | सोऽस्य वज्रेण तान्याशु शिरांसि त्रीण्यथाछिदत् ||
text: Now Indra became aware that the seer (Trisiras) had been sent by the Asuras among the gods. He then with his bolt quickly struck off a those three heads of his.

sanskrit_iast: tasya yatsomapānaṃ tu mukhaṃ so'bhūtkapiñjalaḥ | kalaviṅkaḥ surāpāṇam annādaṃ tittiristvabhūt ||
meaning: तस्य यत्सोमपानं तु मुखं सोऽभूत्कपिञ्जलः | कलविङ्कः सुरापाणम् अन्नादं तित्तिरिस्त्वभूत् ||
text: The mouth with which he drank Soma became a francoline partridge (kapinjala); that with which he drank Sura (became) a sparrow (kalavinka); while that with which he ate food became a partridge (tittiri).

sanskrit_iast: taṃ vāgabhyavadadbrāhmī brahmahāsi śatakrato | prapannaṃ hatavānyasmād viśvarūpaṃ parāṅmukham ||
meaning: तं वागभ्यवदद्ब्राह्मी ब्रह्महासि शतक्रतो | प्रपन्नं हतवान्यस्माद् विश्वरूपं पराङ्मुखम् ||
text: Him (Indra) divine (brahmi) Speech (vac) addressed: 'Thou art Brahman-slayer, Lord of a hundred powers (satakratu), since thou hast slain Visvarupa who sought refuge (prapanna) with averted face.'

sanskrit_iast: tamabhyasiñcatsūktena ṛṣirāpa iti svayam | sindhudvīpo'panuttyarthaṃ tasyāślīlasya pāpmanaḥ ||
meaning: तमभ्यसिञ्चत्सूक्तेन ऋषिराप इति स्वयम् | सिन्धुद्वीपोऽपनुत्त्यर्थं तस्याश्लीलस्य पाप्मनः ||
text: Him (Indra) the seer Sindhudvipa a himself besprinkled, to the accompaniment of the hymn (suktena) 'O Waters' (apah: x. 9), for the removal of that unpropitious sin.

sanskrit_iast: maithunārthamabhīpsantīṃ pratyācaṣṭe yamī yamaḥ | tado ciditi saṃvādo vivasvatsutayostayoḥ ||
meaning: मैथुनार्थमभीप्सन्तीं प्रत्याचष्टे यमी यमः | तदो चिदिति संवादो विवस्वत्सुतयोस्तयोः ||
text: Yama rejects Yami who solicits him with a view to sexual intercourse: the dialogue, 'Hither, indeed' (o cit: x. 10), of those two children of Vivasvat is (descriptive of) that. tado ciditi Am', o citsakhayam (the fuller pratika) B.

sanskrit_iast: vṛṣāgneye havirdhāne yuje vāmatra saṃstute | pareyivāṃsamityatra stūyate madhyamo yamaḥ ||
meaning: वृषाग्नेये हविर्धाने युजे वामत्र संस्तुते | परेयिवांसमित्यत्र स्तूयते मध्यमो यमः ||
text: The two (hymns beginning) 'The bull' (vrsa: x. 11, 12) are addressed to Agni. In the hymn (atra) 'I yoke for you' (yuje vam: x. 13) the two oblation carts are praised together. In 'Him who has passed away' (pareyivamsam: x. 14) the Middle Yama a is praised.

sanskrit_iast: atharvāṇo'tha bhṛgavo'ṅgirasaḥ pitaraḥ saha | ṣaṣṭyāṃ devagaṇāstatra saṃstūyante dyubhaktayaḥ ||
meaning: अथर्वाणोऽथ भृगवोऽङ्गिरसः पितरः सह | षष्ट्यां देवगणास्तत्र संस्तूयन्ते द्युभक्तयः ||
text: Then the Atharvans, the Bhrgus, the Angirases, the Fathers are praised together in the sixth (stanza) there (x. 14. 6), as groups of gods (devagana) connected with heaven (dyubhakti).

sanskrit_iast: pitṛbhiścāṅgirobhiśca saṃstuto dṛśyate yamaḥ | mantreṣu bahuśaḥ pāde vivasvantaṃ pitā hi saḥ ||
meaning: पितृभिश्चाङ्गिरोभिश्च संस्तुतो दृश्यते यमः | मन्त्रेषु बहुशः पादे विवस्वन्तं पिता हि सः ||
text: Yama is frequently seen praised with the Fathers and the Angirases in the formulas; for in the verse 'Vivasvat' (vivasvantam x. 14. 5) he (himself appears as) Father.

sanskrit_iast: saṃskāryapretasaṃyuktaiḥ pitṛbhi stūyate yamaḥ | prehi prehiti tisṛṣu pretāśiṣa udāhṛtāḥ ||
meaning: संस्कार्यप्रेतसंयुक्तैः पितृभि स्तूयते यमः | प्रेहि प्रेहिति तिसृषु प्रेताशिष उदाहृताः ||
text: Yama is praised with the Fathers in conjunction with the deceased man who is to be hallowed (samskarya). In the three (stanzas) Go forth, go forth' (prehi prehi: x. 14. 7-9) prayers for the deceased man are uttered.

sanskrit_iast: pitṝṇāṃ hi patirdevo yamastasmātsa sūktabhāk | ati drava tṛce śvānau paraṃ pitryamudīratām ||
meaning: पितॄणां हि पतिर्देवो यमस्तस्मात्स सूक्तभाक् | अति द्रव तृचे श्वानौ परं पित्र्यमुदीरताम् ||
text: The god Yama is Lord of the Fathers; therefore he owns the hymn (sukta-bhaj). In the triplet 'Run past' (ati drava: x. 14. 10-12) the two dogs (are praised). The following (hymn) 'Let them arise' (ud iratam: x. 15) is addressed to the Fathers.

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa tu sūktena śmaśāne karma śaṃsati | pitṛdevāsurāṇāṃ ca abhavannagnayastrayaḥ | havyakavyavahau cobhau saharakṣāśca nāma yaḥ ||
meaning: उत्तरेण तु सूक्तेन श्मशाने कर्म शंसति | पितृदेवासुराणां च अभवन्नग्नयस्त्रयः | हव्यकव्यवहौ चोभौ सहरक्षाश्च नाम यः ||
text: But with the following hymn (the seer) proclaims the rite in the burning ground. There were three Agnis belonging (respectively) to the Fathers, x. 17 the Gods, and the Asuras: the two who bear oblations (havya) and food offerings (kavya) and he who is called Saharaksas.

sanskrit_iast: tatra mainamiti tvetat kavyavāhanasaṃstutiḥ | itarāṇi tu daivasya stutirnāsyāsurasya ca ||
meaning: तत्र मैनमिति त्वेतत् कव्यवाहनसंस्तुतिः | इतराणि तु दैवस्य स्तुतिर्नास्यासुरस्य च ||
text: Now with regard to these (tatra) the (hymn) 'Not him' (mainam x. 16) is (in) praise of the bearer of food offerings (kavya). Other (hymns), however, are (in) praise of the divine (Agni), not of this one (connected with the Fathers), nor of the demoniac one (asura).

sanskrit_iast: abhavanmithunaṃ tvaṣṭuḥ saraṇyūstriśirāḥ saha | sa vai saraṇyūṃ prāyacchat svayameva vivasvate ||
meaning: अभवन्मिथुनं त्वष्टुः सरण्यूस्त्रिशिराः सह | स वै सरण्यूं प्रायच्छत् स्वयमेव विवस्वते ||
text: Tvastra had twin children, Saranyu as well as Trisiras. He himself gave Saranyu in marriage to Vivasvat. trisirah saha hm'bfks ( Rg-veda), (0yusa )

sanskrit_iast: tataḥ saraṇyvāṃ jajñāte yamasyayau vivasvataḥ | tau cāpyubhau yamāveva jyāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu vai yamaḥ ||
meaning: ततः सरण्य्वां जज्ञाते यमस्ययौ विवस्वतः | तौ चाप्युभौ यमावेव ज्यायांस्ताभ्यां तु वै यमः ||
text: Then Yama and Yami were begotten on Saranyu by Vivasvat. And these two also were twins, but the elder of the two was Yama.

sanskrit_iast: .. iti vṛhaddevatāyāṃ ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ ||
meaning: .. इति वृहद्देवतायां षष्ठोऽध्यायः ||

sanskrit_iast: suṣṭvā bhartuḥ parokṣaṃ tu saraṇyūḥ sadṛśīṃ striyam | nikṣipya mithunaṃ tasyām aśvā bhūtvāpacakrame ||
meaning: सुष्ट्वा भर्तुः परोक्षं तु सरण्यूः सदृशीं स्त्रियम् | निक्षिप्य मिथुनं तस्याम् अश्वा भूत्वापचक्रमे ||
text: Now Saranyu having created, in the absence of her husband, a female similar (to herself) and having entrusted to her the pair (of children), turned herself into a mare and departed.

sanskrit_iast: avijñānādvivasvāṃstu tasyāmajanayanmanum | rājarṣirabhavatso'pi vivasvāniva tejasā ||
meaning: अविज्ञानाद्विवस्वांस्तु तस्यामजनयन्मनुम् | राजर्षिरभवत्सोऽपि विवस्वानिव तेजसा ||
text: But Vivasvat, in ignorance (of this ), begot Manu on that (substitute). He (Manu) became a royal seer, like Vivasvat in brilliance. tasyamajanayan m'bfkrns, tasyam prajanayan hd.

sanskrit_iast: sa vijñāya tvapakrāntāṃ saraṇyūmaśvarūpiṇīm | tvaṣṭrīṃ prati jagāmāśu vājī bhūtvā salakṣaṇaḥ ||
meaning: स विज्ञाय त्वपक्रान्तां सरण्यूमश्वरूपिणीम् | त्वष्ट्रीं प्रति जगामाशु वाजी भूत्वा सलक्षणः ||
text: When, however, he (Vivasvat) had become aware that Saranyu had departed in the shape of a mare, he quickly went after the daughter of Tvastr, having turned himself into a horse with similar characteristics (to hers).

sanskrit_iast: saraṇyūśca vivasvantaṃ viditvā hayarūpiṇam | maithunāyopacakrāma tāṃ ca tatrāruroha saḥ ||
meaning: सरण्यूश्च विवस्वन्तं विदित्वा हयरूपिणम् | मैथुनायोपचक्राम तां च तत्रारुरोह सः ||
text: And Saranyu, recognizing Vivasvat in the form of a steed, approached him for sexual intercourse, and he covered her there. saranyusca Am', saranyustam Bn, sarabyustu s, saranyusca s (Atharva-veda).

sanskrit_iast: tatastayostu vegena śukraṃ tadapatadbhuvi | upājighracca sā tvaśvā tacchukraṃ garbhakāmyayā ||
meaning: ततस्तयोस्तु वेगेन शुक्रं तदपतद्भुवि | उपाजिघ्रच्च सा त्वश्वा तच्छुक्रं गर्भकाम्यया ||
text: Then in their agitation the semen fell on the ground. And the mare, through desire of offspring, smelt the semen. vegena MSS. rs, yogena 8 (Atharva-veda).

sanskrit_iast: āghātamātrācchukrāttu kumārau saṃbabhūvatuḥ | nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca yau stutāvaśvināviti ||
meaning: आघातमात्राच्छुक्रात्तु कुमारौ संबभूवतुः | नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च यौ स्तुतावश्विनाविति ||
text: Now from the semen which had just been smelt there came into being two youths, Nasatya and Dasra, who are praised as 'Asvins'. aghratamatracchukrattu rnf (°chu ° f), °matrachakrattu, °macasuklattu h, °matra- sukratu, °matrakukra hai, aghranamatracchukram tat s.

sanskrit_iast: itihāsamimaṃ yāskaḥ saraṇyūdevate dvṛce | vivasvataśca tvaṣṭuśca tvaṣṭeti saha manyate ||
meaning: इतिहासमिमं यास्कः सरण्यूदेवते द्वृचे | विवस्वतश्च त्वष्टुश्च त्वष्टेति सह मन्यते ||
text: Yaska regards this as a story a of Vivasvat and Tvastr together in the couplet 'Tvastr' (tvasta: x. 17. 1, 2) which has Saranyu for its deity. a

sanskrit_iast: pūṣeti pādau pauṣṇau dvāv āgneyāvuttarau tu yau | syāttṛtīyo'pi vā pauṣṇastisraścānyāḥ parāstu yāḥ ||
meaning: पूषेति पादौ पौष्णौ द्वाव् आग्नेयावुत्तरौ तु यौ | स्यात्तृतीयोऽपि वा पौष्णस्तिस्रश्चान्याः परास्तु याः ||
text: The two verses (beginning) Pusan' (pusa: x. 17. 3) are addressed to Pusan, but the two next (3) to Agni; even the third (3) may optionally (va) be addressed to Pusan; and the other three (stanzas) which follow (4-6) are also (addressed to him).

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ stutistvṛgatraikā tṛcātsārasvatātparā | stutaḥ parokṣaḥ somastu drapsa ityuttare tṛce ||
meaning: अपां स्तुतिस्त्वृगत्रैका तृचात्सारस्वतात्परा | स्तुतः परोक्षः सोमस्तु द्रप्स इत्युत्तरे तृचे ||
text: But one (stanza) in this hymn (atra), which follows the triplet addressed to Sarasvati (7-9), is (in) praise of the Waters (10), while in the next triplet, 'The drop' (drapsah: 11-13), Soma is praised indirectly (paroksa).

sanskrit_iast: abdevatāśīrvādo vā payasvatyuttarā tu yā | catasrastāstutirmṛtyor antye klṛptāśca karmaṇi ||
meaning: अब्देवताशीर्वादो वा पयस्वत्युत्तरा तु या | चतस्रस्तास्तुतिर्मृत्योर् अन्त्ये क्लृप्ताश्च कर्मणि ||
text: But the next (stanza), 'Rich in milk' (payasvati: 14)a, has the waters for its deities or is a benediction. The (next) four (stanzas: x. 18. 1-4) are (in) praise of Death and are applicable (klpta) in the funeral (antya) ceremony.

sanskrit_iast: mṛtaśiṣṭebhya āśāste ime jyogjīvanaṃ punaḥ | imaṃ jīvebhya āśāste tebhyaḥ paridhikarmaṇi ||
meaning: मृतशिष्टेभ्य आशास्ते इमे ज्योग्जीवनं पुनः | इमं जीवेभ्य आशास्ते तेभ्यः परिधिकर्मणि ||
text: The (stanza) 'These' (ime: x. 18. 3) prays for long life for those who have escaped death; For the living this' (imam jivebhyah: 4) again prays (for it) for them in the ceremony with the barrier (paridhi)a.

sanskrit_iast: yathā dhātryuttarā tvāṣṭrī tato yānyā imāstviti | strīṇāmāśiṣamāśāste tayaivāñjanakarmaṇi ||
meaning: यथा धात्र्युत्तरा त्वाष्ट्री ततो यान्या इमास्त्विति | स्त्रीणामाशिषमाशास्ते तयैवाञ्जनकर्मणि ||
text: 'As' (yatha: x. 18. 5) is addressed to Dhatr; the next to Tvastr (6), then with another (7), 'These wives' (imah), he (the seer) utters a prayer for the women in the ceremony with collyrium (anjana). tayaivanjanakarmani B, taya paridhikarmani A: the latter reading is probably due to a clerical error repeating the last word of the preceding sloka, which in that case (though occurring in B only) must have been original. The preceding sloka mentions the stanza which refers to the paridhi, the present sloka mentions the one which refers to anjana.This sloka is wanting in

sanskrit_iast: udīrṣva nārītyanayā mṛtaṃ patnyanurohati | bhrātā kanīyānpretasya nigadya pratiṣedhati ||
meaning: उदीर्ष्व नारीत्यनया मृतं पत्न्यनुरोहति | भ्राता कनीयान्प्रेतस्य निगद्य प्रतिषेधति ||
text: With the (stanza) 'Rise up, O woman' (ud irsva nari: x. 18. 8) the wife ascends (the funeral pyre) after her dead (husband). The younger brother of the departed, repeating (the stanza), prohibits (her). x.

sanskrit_iast: kuryādetatkarma hotā devaro na bhavedyadi | pretānugamanaṃ na syād iti brāhmaṇaśāsanāt ||
meaning: कुर्यादेतत्कर्म होता देवरो न भवेद्यदि | प्रेतानुगमनं न स्याद् इति ब्राह्मणशासनात् ||
text: The Hotr ought to perform this rite, should there be no brother-in-law, because Brahmana enjoins that (the widow) should not follow the departed (husband). This sloka is not found in A, but in B and

sanskrit_iast: varṇānāmitareṣāṃ ca strīdharmo'yaṃ bhavenna vā | śāntyarthaṃ dhanurādāne pretasyarcaṃ dhanurjapet | yasmādetāḥ prayujyante śmaśāne cāntyakarmaṇi ||
meaning: वर्णानामितरेषां च स्त्रीधर्मोऽयं भवेन्न वा | शान्त्यर्थं धनुरादाने प्रेतस्यर्चं धनुर्जपेत् | यस्मादेताः प्रयुज्यन्ते श्मशाने चान्त्यकर्मणि ||
text: This law regarding women may or may not apply to the other castes. In taking the bow (from the hand) of the departed man, one should mutter (the stanza) The bow' (dhanuh: x. 18. 9) a for the sake of averting evil. And because these (stanzas) are employed on the burning ground at the funeral ceremony, The first line of 15 is found in B and

sanskrit_iast: tasmādvadettṛcasvāsya devatāṃ mṛtyumeva tu | mantreṣu hyanirukteṣu devatāṃ karmato vadet ||
meaning: तस्माद्वदेत्तृचस्वास्य देवतां मृत्युमेव तु | मन्त्रेषु ह्यनिरुक्तेषु देवतां कर्मतो वदेत् ||

sanskrit_iast: mantreṣu hyanirukteṣu devatāṃ karmato vadet || mantrataḥ karmataścaiva prajāpatirasaṃbhave | parāścatasro yāstvatra upa sarpeti pārthivī ||
meaning: मन्त्रेषु ह्यनिरुक्तेषु देवतां कर्मतो वदेत् || मन्त्रतः कर्मतश्चैव प्रजापतिरसंभवे | पराश्चतस्रो यास्त्वत्र उप सर्पेति पार्थिवी ||
text: When there is lack (of a deity) from the (evidence of the) formula and the ceremony as well, Prajapati is (the deity). Now as to the following four (stanzas: x. 18. 10-13) here, 'Approach' (upa sarpa: 10) is addressed to the Earth.

sanskrit_iast: tāsāṃ prayogaḥ pretasya asthisaṃcayakarmaṇi | pratīcīne yathāhāni apahṛtyetarāṇi tu ||
meaning: तासां प्रयोगः प्रेतस्य अस्थिसंचयकर्मणि | प्रतीचीने यथाहानि अपहृत्येतराणि तु ||
text: Their application is in the ceremony of collecting the bones a of the departed. Now with the last (stanza) 'In the future' (praticine: x. 18. 14) he (the seer) expresses a prayer (in saying), 'As having taken away (my) other days, the Fathers placed (me) in (past) days, B (so) they also restored me, about to die (prayantam), to life in days to come'. B is: 18 cd follows the reading of Am1 (for,

sanskrit_iast: ahaḥsu pitaro dadhur ityāśāste'ntyayāśiṣaḥ | ahaḥ svāgāmiṣu ca māṃ prayantaṃ samajīvayan ||
meaning: अहःसु पितरो दधुर् इत्याशास्तेऽन्त्ययाशिषः | अहः स्वागामिषु च मां प्रयन्तं समजीवयन् ||

sanskrit_iast: ni vartadhvamitīdaṃ tu gavāṃ kecidapāṃ viduḥ | ardharcaḥ prathamāyāstu agnīṣomīya uttaraḥ ||
meaning: नि वर्तध्वमितीदं तु गवां केचिदपां विदुः | अर्धर्चः प्रथमायास्तु अग्नीषोमीय उत्तरः ||
text: Now the (hymn) Turn back' (ni vartadhvam: x. 19) is (in praise) of Cows; some regard it as (in praise) of the Waters. The latter hemistich of the first (stanza: 1°) is, however, addressed to Agni-Soma.

sanskrit_iast: aindrī ṣaṣṭhī dvitīyāyām ubhau devau nipātitau | daśākṣaraṃ tu śāntyarthaṃ mānasaṃ sūktamucyate ||
meaning: ऐन्द्री षष्ठी द्वितीयायाम् उभौ देवौ निपातितौ | दशाक्षरं तु शान्त्यर्थं मानसं सूक्तमुच्यते ||
text: The sixth (stanza) is addressed to Indra (x. 19. 6), while in the second both the gods a are incidentally mentioned (2). Now the hymn which contains a line of ten syllables (x. 20. 1) is described as intended to avert evil (and) as connected with mind (manasa). suktamucyate Am', suktamuttaram B. a 'Both the gods' (ubhau devau) is rather vague: the two mentioned in the second stanza are Indra and Agni. The Sarvanukramani makes no reference to the deities of Rg-veda x. 19. 2 and 6. Meyer, Rgvidhana, p. xxviii, thinks this line is here regarded This hymn begins with a single verse instead of a stanza: as a whole hymn. b bhadram no api vataya manah. The Sarvanukramani remarks: adya ekapada, pada eva va santyarthah. On this pada cp. Oldenberg, Prolegomena, p. 511. 21°=Rgvidhana iii. 8. 6ª; cp. the whole sloka there: dasaksaram tu Santyartham bhadram na iti samsmaret; nityam japec chucir bhutva: manasam vindate sukham.

sanskrit_iast: trīṇyaindrāṇi kuhetyatra āgneyābhyāṃ parāṇi tu | tṛco'trāstyāśvinastveka aindrāṇāmuttame yuvam ||
meaning: त्रीण्यैन्द्राणि कुहेत्यत्र आग्नेयाभ्यां पराणि तु | तृचोऽत्रास्त्याश्विनस्त्वेक ऐन्द्राणामुत्तमे युवम् ||
text: Now here after two hymns addressed to Agni (x. 20, 21) there follow three addressed to Indra (beginning) 'Where?' (kuha: x. 22-24). Now in the last of the hymns to Indra there is one triplet 'Ye two' (yuvam: x. 24. 4-6) addressed to the Asvins.

sanskrit_iast: bhadraṃ saumyaṃ pra hi pauṣṇaṃ trīṇyaindrāṇi parāṇyasat | teṣāmādyena mattaḥ san svāni karmāṇi śaṃsati ||
meaning: भद्रं सौम्यं प्र हि पौष्णं त्रीण्यैन्द्राणि पराण्यसत् | तेषामाद्येन मत्तः सन् स्वानि कर्माणि शंसति ||
text: 'Happy' (bhadram: x. 25) is addressed to Soma; 'Forth indeed' (pra hi: x. 26) is addressed to Pusan. The three following (beginning) 'It shall be' (asat: x. 27-29) are addressed to Indra: with the first (27) of these (Indra), being exhilarated, proclaims his deeds; II.

sanskrit_iast: yathā carati bhūteṣu yathā varṣati pāti ca || sūkte tadasminnaṣṭābhir ṛgbhiruktamabhūrviti ||
meaning: यथा चरति भूतेषु यथा वर्षति पाति च || सूक्ते तदस्मिन्नष्टाभिर् ऋग्भिरुक्तमभूर्विति ||

sanskrit_iast: sapteti maruta stauti stauti vajramṛguttarā | agnimindraṃ ca somaṃ ca pīvānaṃ meṣamarcati .. ||
meaning: सप्तेति मरुत स्तौति स्तौति वज्रमृगुत्तरा | अग्निमिन्द्रं च सोमं च पीवानं मेषमर्चति .. ||
text: (The stanza) 'Seven' (sapta: x. 27. 15) praises the Maruts, the next stanza (16) praises the Bolt; (the stanza) 'The fatted ram' (pivanam mesam: 17) adores Agni, Indra and Soma:

sanskrit_iast: pūrvo'rdharco'parastasyāḥ parjanyaṃ vāyunā saha | vi krośanāsa ityagnim uttarā sūryameva tu ||
meaning: पूर्वोऽर्धर्चोऽपरस्तस्याः पर्जन्यं वायुना सह | वि क्रोशनास इत्यग्निम् उत्तरा सूर्यमेव तु ||
text: (that is) its first hemistich (does so: 17 ab), while its second one (adores) Parjanya with Vayu (17 cd). 'Crying aloud' (vi kro- sanasah: 18) (praises) Agni, but the next (stanza) Surya (19). rdharco'paras B, rdharcottarasa Am'.

sanskrit_iast: etau me'yaṃ ya ityete stutiścaivendravajrayoḥ | vṛkṣevṛkṣe dhanuścendraṃ devānāmiti tu trayaḥ ||
meaning: एतौ मेऽयं य इत्येते स्तुतिश्चैवेन्द्रवज्रयोः | वृक्षेवृक्षे धनुश्चेन्द्रं देवानामिति तु त्रयः ||
text: 'These two of mine' (etau me: x. 27. 20) and 'This which' (ayam yah: 21)-these two (stanzas) are (in) praise of Indra and the Bolt; and 'To every tree' (vrkse-vrkse: 22) (praises) the Bow of Indra. But (in) 'Of the Gods' (devanam: 23) the three 27 ab follows the reading of

sanskrit_iast: śītoṣṇavarṣadātāraḥ parjanyānilabhāskarāḥ | antye sūryonilau cobhau stūyete ca pade saha ||

sanskrit_iast: sā te jīvāturityasyām indro vā sūrya eva vā | viśvo anyastu saṃvāda ṛṣeḥ śakrasya caiva hi ||
meaning: सा ते जीवातुरित्यस्याम् इन्द्रो वा सूर्य एव वा | विश्वो अन्यस्तु संवाद ऋषेः शक्रस्य चैव हि ||
text: In the (stanza) 'This is thy life' (sa te jivatuh: 24) either Indra or Surya (is praised). But 'Every other' (visvo hy anyah: x. 28) is a dialogue of the seer and of Sakra (Indra).

sanskrit_iast: yugmāḥ śakrasya vijñeyā vasukrasyetarā ṛcaḥ | snuṣendrasyāgatāndevān dṛṣṭvā śakramanāgatam ||
meaning: युग्माः शक्रस्य विज्ञेया वसुक्रस्येतरा ऋचः | स्नुषेन्द्रस्यागतान्देवान् दृष्ट्वा शक्रमनागतम् ||
text: The even (stanzas) are to be recognized as Sakra's, the other stanzas as Vasukra's. B The daughter-in-law of Indra, seeing the gods had come, but Sakra had not come 3098 follows the reading of B; the reading of Am1 is: yugma eva tu sakrasya ayugma eva tu

sanskrit_iast: yajñaṃ parokṣavatprāha śvaśuro nāgato mama | yadyāgacched bhakṣayetsa dhānāḥ somaṃ pibedapi ||
meaning: यज्ञं परोक्षवत्प्राह श्वशुरो नागतो मम | यद्यागच्छेद् भक्षयेत्स धानाः सोमं पिबेदपि ||

sanskrit_iast: iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā tatkṣaṇādetya vajradhṛk | tiṣṭhanvedyāmuttarasyām uccairāha sa roruvat ||
meaning: इति तस्या वचः श्रुत्वा तत्क्षणादेत्य वज्रधृक् | तिष्ठन्वेद्यामुत्तरस्याम् उच्चैराह स रोरुवत् ||
text: The Bolt-bearer on hearing this speech of hers, came that very moment, and standing on the northern altar (uttara vedi), said aloud: 'He bellowing loud' (sa roruvat: x. 28. 2). r.

sanskrit_iast: tṛtīyayā caturthyā ca pra devatretyapāṃ stutau | apāṃnapādityanena nāmnāgnirmadhyama stutaḥ ||
meaning: तृतीयया चतुर्थ्या च प्र देवत्रेत्यपां स्तुतौ | अपांनपादित्यनेन नाम्नाग्निर्मध्यम स्तुतः ||
text: In the praise of Waters (beginning) 'Forth to the gods' (pra devatra: x. 30) the Middle Agni is praised by the name of 260 "Child of Waters' (apam napat) with the third and the fourth (stanza).

sanskrit_iast: eti yadvaiśvadevaṃ tu tasya pretyaindramuttaram | vaiśvadevī pra metyekā saṃ metyendro dvṛcaḥ paraḥ ||
meaning: एति यद्वैश्वदेवं तु तस्य प्रेत्यैन्द्रमुत्तरम् | वैश्वदेवी प्र मेत्येका सं मेत्येन्द्रो द्वृचः परः ||
text: Now (the hymn) which (begins) Hither' (a: x. 31) is addressed to the All-gods; the one next to that, 'Forth' (pra: x. 32), is addressed to Indra. One (stanza) 'Onward me' (pra ma x. 33. 1) is addressed to the All-gods; the following couplet 'Together me' (sam ma: 2, 3) is addressed to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: kuruśravaṇamarcataḥ pare dve trāsadasyavam | mṛte mitrātithau rājñi tannapātamṛṣiḥ paraiḥ ||
meaning: कुरुश्रवणमर्चतः परे द्वे त्रासदस्यवम् | मृते मित्रातिथौ राज्ञि तन्नपातमृषिः परैः ||
text: Cp. Rg-veda x. 33. 7 upamasravo napan mitratither ihi. See also Sarvanukramani: mrte mitralithau rajni.. rsir upamasravasam putram asya (kurusravanasya) vyasokayat.

sanskrit_iast: upamaśravasaṃ yasya caturbhiḥ sa vyaśokayat | prāvepā iti sūktaṃ yat tadakṣastutirucyate ||
meaning: उपमश्रवसं यस्य चतुर्भिः स व्यशोकयत् | प्रावेपा इति सूक्तं यत् तदक्षस्तुतिरुच्यते ||

sanskrit_iast: atrākṣāndvādaśī stauti navamyādyā ca saptamī | trayodaśī kṛṣiṃ stauti kitavaṃ cānuśāsati | akṣāṃstu śeṣā nindanti abudhraṃ vaiśvadevate ||
meaning: अत्राक्षान्द्वादशी स्तौति नवम्याद्या च सप्तमी | त्रयोदशी कृषिं स्तौति कितवं चानुशासति | अक्षांस्तु शेषा निन्दन्ति अबुध्रं वैश्वदेवते ||
text: Here the twelfth (stanza) praises the Dice, the ninth, the first, and the seventh (x. 34. 1, 7, 9, 12). A The thirteenth a praises tillage (13) and admonishes the gambler. But the remaining (stanzas) blame the Dice. Two (hymns x. 44 beginning) 'They are awake' (abudhram: x. 35, 36) are addressed to the All-gods.

sanskrit_iast: sāvitrameke manyante maho agne stavaṃ param | ācāryāḥ śaunako yāsko gālavaścottamāmṛcam ||
meaning: सावित्रमेके मन्यन्ते महो अग्ने स्तवं परम् | आचार्याः शौनको यास्को गालवश्चोत्तमामृचम् ||
text: Some consider the praise at the end (para), 'Of the great Agni' (maho agneh: x. 36. 12-14), to be addressed to Savitr; the teachers Saunaka, Yaska, and Galava (consider) the last (14) stanza (to be such). This sloka is not found in A, but in B and

sanskrit_iast: namaḥ sauryamaindramasmin saurye ṣaṣṭyā tu yā stutāḥ | nipātinyastāḥ sūktānte vaiśvadevo'tra tu dvṛcaḥ ||
meaning: नमः सौर्यमैन्द्रमस्मिन् सौर्ये षष्ट्या तु या स्तुताः | निपातिन्यस्ताः सूक्तान्ते वैश्वदेवोऽत्र तु द्वृचः ||
text: 'Obeisance' (namah: x. 37) is addressed to Surya, 'In this' (asmin x. 38) to Indra. But (the deities) who are praised in the sixth (stanza) of the hymn to Surya (x. 37. 6) are incidental; at the end of this (atra) hymn there is a couplet addressed to the All-gods (x. 37. II, 12).

sanskrit_iast: āśvināni tu yastrīṇi aindrāṇyasteva su pra ca | aindrāṇāmuttamāyāstu stuto'rdharca bṛhaspatiḥ ||
meaning: आश्विनानि तु यस्त्रीणि ऐन्द्राण्यस्तेव सु प्र च | ऐन्द्राणामुत्तमायास्तु स्तुतोऽर्धर्च बृहस्पतिः ||
text: Now there are three hymns addressed to the Asvins (beginning) Which' (yah: x. 39-41), and there are (three) addressed to Indra (beginning) 'As the archer far' (asteva su 262 pra- x. 42-44), but in a hemistich (116) of the last stanza of the Indra hymns (42-44) Brhaspati b is praised.

sanskrit_iast: pare divasparyāgneye prathamasyottamena tu | dyāvāpṛthivyau viśve ca paccho'rdharccena saṃstutāḥ ||

meaning: आसीत्काक्षीवती घोषा पापरोगेण दुर्भगा | उवास षष्टि वर्षाणि पितुरेव गृहे पुरा ||

sanskrit_iast: ātasthe mahatīṃ cintāṃ na putro na patirmama | jarāṃ prāptāṃ mudhātasmāt prapadye'haṃ śubhaspatī ||

text: She fell into great grief (thinking), 'Without son or husband I have reached old age in vain; I (will) therefore resort to the Lords of Light (subhaspati). mahatim cintam fm'bn, mahati cinta, mahi cimta .

text: Since my father, by propitiating them, obtained youth, long life, health, power, poison for slaying all

meaning: रूपवतां च सौभाग्यम् अहं तस्य सुता यदि | समापि मन्त्राः प्रादुःस्युर् यैस्तोष्येते मयाश्विनौ ||
text: I, his daughter, (would obtain) beauty and good fortune, if to me also were revealed formulas in which the Asvins shall be praised & by me.' rupavattam ca rn, rupavantam ca 1, rupatta caiva f, rupata caiva m k.

sanskrit_iast: cintayantīti sūkte dve yo vāṃ pari dadarśa sā | stutau tāvaśvinau devau prītau tasyā bhagāntaram ||
meaning: चिन्तयन्तीति सूक्ते द्वे यो वां परि ददर्श सा | स्तुतौ तावश्विनौ देवौ प्रीतौ तस्या भगान्तरम् ||
text: As she reffected thus, she saw the two hymns 'Your encircling' (yo vama pari-: x. 39, 40). The two divine ASvins being praised, were pleased. Entering her organ (bhaga) they made her ageless, free from disease, and beautiful (subhaga). They gave her a husband and the sage Suhastya as a son. 46.

sanskrit_iast: praviśya vijarārogāṃ subhagāṃ cakratuśca tau | bhartāraṃ dadatustasyai suhastyaṃ ca sutaṃ munim ||

sanskrit_iast: dadatustatsuparṇābhyāṃ yannāsatyeti kīrtyate | kākṣīvatyai ca ghoṣāyai na tasyāmājuro'nayā ||
meaning: ददतुस्तत्सुपर्णाभ्यां यन्नासत्येति कीर्त्यते | काक्षीवत्यै च घोषायै न तस्यामाजुरोऽनया ||
text: What the ' Nasatyas' by means of their two winged steeds (suparnabhyam) & gave to Ghosa, daughter of Kaksivat, is proclaimed by the (stanzas), ' Not of that' (na tasya: x. 40. 11) (and) - Of her that grows old at home' (amajurah: x. 39.3).

sanskrit_iast: prājāpatyāsurī tvāsīd vikuṇṭhā nāma nāmataḥ | sechantīndrasamaṃ putraṃ tepe'tha sumahattapaḥ ||
meaning: प्राजापत्यासुरी त्वासीद् विकुण्ठा नाम नामतः | सेछन्तीन्द्रसमं पुत्रं तेपेऽथ सुमहत्तपः ||
text: There was an Asuri, daughter of Prajapati, Vikuntha by name. She, desiring a son like Indra, performed very severe austerities

sanskrit_iast: sā prajāpatitaḥ kārmāṃllebhe'tha vividhān varān | tasyāṃ cendraḥ svayaṃ jajñe jiyāṃsurdaityadānavān ||
meaning: सा प्रजापतितः कार्मांल्लेभेऽथ विविधान् वरान् | तस्यां चेन्द्रः स्वयं जज्ञे जियांसुर्दैत्यदानवान् ||
text: She then obtained from Prajapati her desires (in the form of) various boons. And Indra himself was born of her, as he wished to slay the Daityas and Danavas.

sanskrit_iast: ekadā dānavaiḥ sārdhaṃ samare samasajyata | jaghāna teṣāṃ navatīr nava sapta ca saptakān ||
meaning: एकदा दानवैः सार्धं समरे समसज्यत | जघान तेषां नवतीर् नव सप्त च सप्तकान् ||
text: Once he was engaged in battle with the Danavas. Of them he slew nine nineties a and seven groups of seven.

sanskrit_iast: bhittvā svabāhuvīryeṇa haimaraupyāyasīḥ purīḥ | hatvā sarvān yathāsthānaṃ pṛthivyādivyavasthitān ||
meaning: भित्त्वा स्वबाहुवीर्येण हैमरौप्यायसीः पुरीः | हत्वा सर्वान् यथास्थानं पृथिव्यादिव्यवस्थितान् ||
text: Having shattered with the might of his arm their citadels of gold, silver, and iron, (and) having slain all (of them) in their respective spheres (yathasthanam), as arrayed on earth and in the other (two worlds). x.

sanskrit_iast: pṛthivyāṃ kālakeyāṃśca paulomāṃścaiva dhanvinaḥ | tāṃśca vyutsādayāmāsa prahlādatanayāndivi ||
meaning: पृथिव्यां कालकेयांश्च पौलोमांश्चैव धन्विनः | तांश्च व्युत्सादयामास प्रह्लादतनयान्दिवि ||
text: On earth he exterminated both the Kalakeyas and the race of Puloma, the archers, and in heaven the notorious (tan) offspring of Prahlada.

sanskrit_iast: rājyaṃ prāpya sa daityeṣu svena vīryeṇa darpitaḥ | devānbādhitumārebhe mohito'suramāyayā ||
meaning: राज्यं प्राप्य स दैत्येषु स्वेन वीर्येण दर्पितः | देवान्बाधितुमारेभे मोहितोऽसुरमायया ||
text: Having obtained sovereignty among the Daityas (and) puffed up with pride by reason of his might, he began to harass the gods, being infatuated by the craft of the Asuras.

sanskrit_iast: bādhyamānāstu tenāpi asureṇāmitaujasā | upādhāvannṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ tatprabodhāya saptagum ||
meaning: बाध्यमानास्तु तेनापि असुरेणामितौजसा | उपाधावन्नृषिश्रेष्ठं तत्प्रबोधाय सप्तगुम् ||
text: Now while they were being harassed by that same Asura of unlimited power, they fled for succour to Saptagu, most excellent of seers, in order that (the latter) should admonish him (Indra).

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣistu saptagurnāma tasyāsītsupriyaḥ sakhā | sa cainamabhituṣṭāva jagṛbhmeti kare spṛśan ||
meaning: ऋषिस्तु सप्तगुर्नाम तस्यासीत्सुप्रियः सखा | स चैनमभितुष्टाव जगृभ्मेति करे स्पृशन् ||
text: Now the seer called Saptagu was a dear friend of his, and (so) he praised him with the (hymn), 'We have grasped' (jagrbhma: x. 47), as he took him by the hand. sa

sanskrit_iast: tataḥ sa buddhvā cātmānaṃ saptagustutiharṣitaḥ | ātmānameva tuṣṭāva ahaṃ bhuvamiti tribhiḥ ||
meaning: ततः स बुद्ध्वा चात्मानं सप्तगुस्तुतिहर्षितः | आत्मानमेव तुष्टाव अहं भुवमिति त्रिभिः ||
text: Then he coming to (buddhva) himself (and) rejoiced at the praise of Saptagu, praised himself with the three (hymns) 'I was' (aham bhuvam: x.

sanskrit_iast: kīrtayansvāni karmāṇi yāni sma kṛtavānpurā | yathākarocca vaidehaṃ vyaṃsaṃ somapatiṃ nṛpam ||
meaning: कीर्तयन्स्वानि कर्माणि यानि स्म कृतवान्पुरा | यथाकरोच्च वैदेहं व्यंसं सोमपतिं नृपम् ||

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭhaśāpādabhavad vaideho nṛpatiḥ purā | indraprasādādīje ca sattraiḥ sārasvatādibhiḥ ||
meaning: वसिष्ठशापादभवद् वैदेहो नृपतिः पुरा | इन्द्रप्रसादादीजे च सत्त्रैः सारस्वतादिभिः ||

sanskrit_iast: prabhūtāṃ śaktimattāṃ ca śatrūṇāmapyapākriyām | nṛṣu sarveṣu caiśvaryaṃ prabhutvaṃ bhuvaneṣu ca | pra vo maha iti tvasyām ātmano vīryamakṣayam ||
meaning: प्रभूतां शक्तिमत्तां च शत्रूणामप्यपाक्रियाम् | नृषु सर्वेषु चैश्वर्यं प्रभुत्वं भुवनेषु च | प्र वो मह इति त्वस्याम् आत्मनो वीर्यमक्षयम् ||
text: The curse of Vasistha, it appears, relegated Vyamsa to a remote Eastern region (Tirhut) beyond the pale of orthodox Brahmanism, but the favour of Indra afterwards enabled him to perform sacrifices on the Sarasvati and so to become a lord of Soma,' like himself (somapati being an epithet of Indra). B 60. and (praising) his great power and his injury to foes, and his sovereignty among all men and his lordship in the worlds; but in the (stanza) Forth to your great' (pra vo mahe: x. 50. 1) his own imperishable might.

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānare gṛhapatau yaviṣṭhe'gnau ca pāvake | vaṣaṭkāreṇa vṛkṇeṣu bhrātṛṣvagnau sahaḥsute ||
meaning: वैश्वानरे गृहपतौ यविष्ठेऽग्नौ च पावके | वषट्कारेण वृक्णेषु भ्रातृष्वग्नौ सहःसुते ||

sanskrit_iast: apacakrāma devebhyaḥ saucīko'gniriti śrutiḥ | sa praviśadapakramya ṛtūnapo vanaspatīn ||
meaning: अपचक्राम देवेभ्यः सौचीकोऽग्निरिति श्रुतिः | स प्रविशदपक्रम्य ऋतूनपो वनस्पतीन् ||
text: Agni Saucika departed from the gods, so Vedic text (relates). He on departing entered the seasons, the waters, (and) the trees.

sanskrit_iast: tato'surāḥ prādurāsan naṣṭe'gnau havyavāhane | te'gnimevānvavaikṣanta devā hatvāsurānyudhi ||

text: Then the Asuras appeared, when Agni the oblation-bearer had vanished. The gods, having slain the Asuras in fight, looked about in quest of Agni.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ tu dūrādyamaścaiva varuṇaścānvapaśyatām | ubhāvenaṃ samādāya devānevābhijagmatuḥ ||

text: Now Yama and Varuna a espied him from afar. Both of them, taking him with them, went to the gods.

sanskrit_iast: dṛṣṭvā devāstvenamūcur agne havyāni no vaha | varān gṛhāṇa cāsmattaś citrabhāno bhajasva naḥ | devayānān sugān pathaḥ kuruṣva sumanāḥ svayam ||

text: On seeing him the gods said : '0 Agni, bear our oblations, and accept boons & from us; do thou, O brilliantly shining one, attend upon us; B do thou thyself graciously make the paths trodden by the gods easy to traverse.'

text: Yaska a and Aupamanyava state these to be the five races. Sakatayana thinks they are the (four) castes with the Nisadas as a fifth.

sanskrit_iast: ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate | hotādhvaryustathodgātā brahmā ceti vadanti tān ||

text: Sakapuni, however, thinks they are the (four) priests (rtvij) and the institutor of the sacrifice (yajamana). B Those (priests) they call Hotr,' 'Adhvaryu,' 'Udgatr,' and 'Brahman.'

sanskrit_iast: cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ | gandharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā ||

text: Eye, ear, mind, speech, and breath, say the theosophists (atmavadin). They are stated to be Gandharvas and Apsarases, Gods, Men, Fathers, and Serpents in the sacred text of the Aitareya Brahmanab_ 'and (continued Agni) whatever other terrestrial creatures (prthivijatah) and other divine beings (devah) there are that receive worship (yajniyah). sanskrit_iast: sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyante hyaitareyake | ye cānye pṛthivījātā devāścānye'tha yajñiyāḥ ||
meaning: सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयन्ते ह्यैतरेयके | ये चान्ये पृथिवीजाता देवाश्चान्येऽथ यज्ञियाः ||

sanskrit_iast: āyurastu ca me dīrghaṃ havīṃṣi vividhāni ca | ariṣṭiḥ pūrvajānāṃ ca bhrātṛṇāmadhvare'dhvare ||
meaning: आयुरस्तु च मे दीर्घं हवींषि विविधानि च | अरिष्टिः पूर्वजानां च भ्रातृणामध्वरेऽध्वरे ||
text: And let me have long life, and various oblations, and let my elder brothers enjoy safety at every sacrifice;

sanskrit_iast: prayājāścānuyājāśca ghṛtaṃ some ca yaḥ paśuḥ | maddaivatyāni vai santu yajño maddevato'stu ca ||

sanskrit_iast: tavāgne yajña ityetat pratyādhi sviṣṭakṛcca saḥ | yasya trīṇi sahasrāṇi nava trīṇi śatāni ca ||
meaning: तवाग्ने यज्ञ इत्येतत् प्रत्याधि स्विष्टकृच्च सः | यस्य त्रीणि सहस्राणि नव त्रीणि शतानि च ||
text: This was accorded (pratyardhi) with (the words) 'Thine, O Agni, the sacrifice' (tavagne yajnah: x. 51. 9); and he (became) Svistakrt (offering right sacrifice), to whom the three thousand, three hundred and nine

sanskrit_iast: triṃśaccaiva tu devānāṃ sarvāmeva varāndaduḥ | tato'gniḥ sumanāḥ prīto viśvedevaiḥ puraskṛtaḥ ||
meaning: त्रिंशच्चैव तु देवानां सर्वामेव वरान्ददुः | ततोऽग्निः सुमनाः प्रीतो विश्वेदेवैः पुरस्कृतः ||

sanskrit_iast: vidhūyāṅgāni yajñeṣu cakre hotramatandritaḥ | bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ proto divyātmā havyavāhanaḥ ||

sanskrit_iast: romāṇi kāśāḥ keśāstu kṛśāḥ kūrmā nakhāni ca | antrāṇi caivāpyavakā majjā sikataśarkarāḥ ||
meaning: रोमाणि काशाः केशास्तु कृशाः कूर्मा नखानि च | अन्त्राणि चैवाप्यवका मज्जा सिकतशर्कराः ||

sanskrit_iast: asṛk pittaṃ ca vividhā dhātavo gairikādayaḥ | evamagniśca devāśca sūktairmahaditi tribhiḥ ||

sanskrit_iast: samūdire pare tvasmād aindre sūkte tu tāṃ su te | vidhuṃ dadrāṇamityasyāṃ sūryācandramasau stutau ||

text: The praise here also appears as of Breath and of Soul. The two (hymns) 'This' (idam: x. 56, 57) are addressed to the Allgods. In the second (57) b there is a triplet (3-5) to Mind (manas).

sanskrit_iast: prathamaindro dvitīyāgneyy antyā tatsomadevatā | api stauti pitṝnetad ārtvijaṃ yattaduttaram ||

B This (hymn) praises the Fathers a also (and) should be recited (in that sense) by priests (artvija). The hymn (beginning) Which' (yat x. 58), coming next after that,

sanskrit_iast: sūktamākhyānasaṃyuktaṃ vaktukāmasya me śṛṇu | saṃmohānnaṣṭasaṃjñasya śatruṇābhihatasya tu ||

sanskrit_iast: jīvāvṛttiḥ subandhorvā yadi vā manasa stavaḥ | rājāsamātiraikṣvākū rathaproṣṭhaḥ purohitān ||
meaning: जीवावृत्तिः सुबन्धोर्वा यदि वा मनस स्तवः | राजासमातिरैक्ष्वाकू रथप्रोष्ठः पुरोहितान् ||

text: Asamati made his domestic priests; for he considered them the best. These two priests having become pigeons and having gone against the

text: And the following (triplet) which, (beginning) 'Let be prolonged' (pra tari: x. 59), they muttered with a view to remedies is the first triplet of the hymn (1-3): it is there meant to drive away (apanodana) Dissolution (nirrti).

sanskrit_iast: trayaḥ pādā mo ṣviti tu saumyā nairṛta uttamaḥ | ṛk saumyā nairṛtī caiṣā asunīte stutiḥ pare ||

text: Now the three verses 'Not at all' (mo su: x. 59. 4 abe) are addressed to Soma, the last (4%) to Nirrtia: this whole stanza being addressed to Soma and Nirrti. The following two (stanzas: 5, 6) are (in) praise of Asuniti. x.

sanskrit_iast: dvṛce tvānumataṃ pādam antyaṃ yāskastu manyate | bhūrdyauḥ somaśca pūṣā ca khaṃ pathyā svastireva ca ||
meaning: द्वृचे त्वानुमतं पादम् अन्त्यं यास्कस्तु मन्यते | भूर्द्यौः सोमश्च पूषा च खं पथ्या स्वस्तिरेव च ||

sanskrit_iast: subandhoreva śāntyarthaṃ punarna ṛci tu smṛtāḥ | tṛcaḥ śamiti rodasyor aindro'rdharcaḥ samityṛci ||
meaning: सुबन्धोरेव शान्त्यर्थं पुनर्न ऋचि तु स्मृताः | तृचः शमिति रोदस्योर् ऐन्द्रोऽर्धर्चः समित्यृचि ||

sanskrit_iast: rapaso nāśanārthaṃ vai tuṣṭuvustyatha rodasī | rapa ityabhidhānaṃ tu gaditaṃ pāpakṛchrayoḥ ||

text: Now they praised the Two Worlds for the destruction of infirmity (rapas): 'infirmity' is stated to be a designation of sin or (bodily) trouble.

sanskrit_iast: ṛgbhireti catasṛbhis tata aikṣvākumastuvan | indra kṣatretyṛcā cāsya stutvāśaṃsiṣurāśiṣaḥ ||

text: Then with the four stanzas 'Hither' (a: x. 60. 1-4) they praised the scion of Iksvaku, and after praising him they uttered prayers for him with the stanza O Indra, dominion' (indra ksatra x. 60. 5).

sanskrit_iast: agastyasyeti mātā ca teṣāṃ tuṣṭāva taṃ nṛpam | stutaḥ sa rājā savrīḻas tasthau gopāyanānabhi ||
meaning: अगस्त्यस्येति माता च तेषां तुष्टाव तं नृपम् | स्तुतः स राजा सव्रीḻअस् तस्थौ गोपायनानभि ||
text: And their mother & praised the king with (the stanza) 'Of Agastya' (agastyasya: x. 60.6).

sanskrit_iast: sūktenāpyastuvannagniṃ dvaipadena yathātriṣu | agnirapyatrabravīdetān aymantaḥ paridhyasuḥ ||

text: As among the Atris a they had also praised Agni with a dvipada hymn (dvaipada), Agni, on his part, said to them, 'Here within the sacrificial barrier' (antahparidhi) b is the spirit suktenapya ° bfkn, suktenatha, suktenaisam Am'.

sanskrit_iast: subandhorasya caikṣvākor mayā gupto hitarthinā | subandhave pradāyāsuṃ jīvetyuktvā ca pāvakaḥ ||

sanskrit_iast: stuto gaupāyanaiḥ prīto jagāma tridivaṃ prati | ayaṃ māteti hṛṣṭāste subandhorasumāhvayan ||
